Bokeon Kwak, researcher at EPFL's Laboratory of Intelligent Systems and Julien Boutonnet, EHL Senior Lecturer of Practical Arts at EHL - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
A Swiss Italian team has created RoboCake, an edible robotic wedding cake that illustrates the advances in robotic food research.
While the idea of creating robots that can be eaten or food that behaves like robots may seem weird, it is a real challenge for the scientific community. As part of the EU-funded RoboFood project, researchers from EPFL and the
Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia
(IIT- Italian Institute of Technology) have collaborated with pastry chefs and food scientists from
EHL in Lausanne
, to marry robotic science and gastronomy. Their project, RoboCake, is being showcased at the Expo 2025 Osaka.
“Robotics and food are two separate worlds,” says Dario Floreano, head of the
Laboratory of Intelligent Systems (LIS)
at EPFL and coordinator of the RoboFood project. “However, merging them offers many advantages, particularly in terms of limiting electronic waste and food waste.” Other applications in the fields of emergency nutrition and health are being considered by scientists. “Edible robots could be used to deliver food to endangered areas, to deliver medicines in innovative ways to people who have difficulty swallowing or to animals, or even to monitor food and its freshness using sensors that can be eaten.
Illustrating robotic food research
Creating edible robots also offers brand new culinary experiences. The RoboCake, a robotic wedding cake, is an innovative demonstration of the progress made by the RoboFood project, which aims to develop a new generation of edible robots and intelligent food.
Edible robotic teddy bears, created by the LIS at EPFL - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
The RoboCake features two completely edible robotic teddy bears, created by the LIS at EPFL. “They are made from gelatin, syrup and colorants,” explains Bokeon Kwak, a researcher at LIS.” They are animated by an internal pneumatic system: when air is injected through dedicated pathways, their heads and arms move.”
These dancing bears, which taste like soft, sweet pomegranate gummies, are not the only special feature of the cake. IIT researchers, coordinated by Mario Caironi, have developed the first edible rechargeable battery, made of vitamin B2, quercetin, activated carbon and chocolate, for the gourmet touch. “These batteries, safe for consumption, can be used to light the LED candles on the cake,” explains Valerio Galli, a PhD student at IIT. "The first flavor you get when you eat them is dark chocolate, followed by a surprising tangy kick, due to the edible electrolyte inside, which lasts a few seconds”. These batteries represent a potential solution to reducing electronic waste, which reaches 40 million tons per year.
Edible dark chocolat batteries - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
The icing on the cake
To ensure these innovations are both appetizing and safe to eat, the engineers teamed up with food experts and pastry chefs from EHL. “Our challenge was to find the best way to showcase the innovations of our two partners, EPFL and IIT, by adding what we do best: indulgence. This is how the RoboCake was born, a true event pastry cake, meeting the challenge of combining technique, electronics, and taste.” says Julien Boutonnet, EHL Senior Lecturer Practical Arts and France’s top distinction, the Meilleur Ouvrier de France (MOF) award for pastry and candymaking.
“This interdisciplinary collaboration paves the way for interactive and delicious gastronomic experiences reminding us that food is a precious resource and possibly reducing overeating”, says Dario Floreano.
Valerio Galli and Julien Boutonnet - 2025 EPFL/Jamani Caillet - CC-BY-SA 4.0
About the RoboFood project
RoboFood is a 3.5-million-euro four-year research project funded by the European Union. Launched in 2021, it brings together scientists from EPFL, IIT, the University of Bristol and the University of Wageningen. The RoboFood project combines food science and robotics in a radically new way to create edible robots and robotized food for food preservation, emergency nutrition, human and veterinary medicine or new culinary experiences.

data.title: The dark side of account bans
data.author: ponco
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了在线账户被封禁的严重影响，特别是Meta旗下服务如Facebook、Instagram和WhatsApp。作者Maddy Miller是一位Minecraft模组开发者，因遭遇用户骚扰而被人恶意举报，导致所有Meta相关账户被永久封禁。尽管作者尝试通过支持渠道解决问题，但毫无进展，最终通过在社交媒体上求助才幸运地恢复账户。文章指出，失去这些账户不仅影响社交联系，还影响日常生活的诸多方面，如与商家沟通和获取信息。这揭示了现代生活中对大公司在线平台的高度依赖，以及当前账户封禁机制存在的问题，呼吁相关机制需要改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta平台（包括Facebook和Instagram）的用户体验、账户封禁问题以及数字服务依赖的争议。

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如chrisldgk）分享了自己在Meta平台上遇到的账户封禁问题，尤其是在经过验证后账户仍被封禁，且申诉无效。这揭示了Meta在处理开发者账户和用户申诉方面的不足。
• yellow_lead指出Instagram在处理广告举报时的无效性，认为平台对举报的处理机制存在问题，可能依赖某种阈值机制来决定是否采取行动。
• db48x对比了不同地区餐馆菜单的数字化情况，指出有些地方依赖Instagram展示菜单，而其他地方则使用传统网页或PDF菜单。j1elo对此表示强烈反对，认为这种“数字化狂热”是愚蠢的，忽视了那些不总是携带高端设备的用户。
• dredmorbius和其他用户（如ValdikSS）建议通过法律途径解决问题，如小额索赔法庭，以及联系消费者保护机构和相关政府代表。他们强调组织和行动的重要性，而不是仅仅在社交媒体上抱怨。
• fweimer和stevage讨论了在不同国家（尤其是澳大利亚）通过法律途径解决账户问题的复杂性，并分享了自己或他人通过特殊渠道恢复账户的经历。
• 一些用户（如n4r9和Rebuff5007）对Meta的申诉机制缺失和用户遭遇的不公正对待表示同情，并质疑为什么没有更健全的法律来保护用户免受永久封禁的影响。
• nickdothutton和maxehmookau批评了当前用户举报和平台处理机制的不足，认为普通用户的举报行为往往不可靠，而平台在处理这些举报时缺乏正当程序。
• antonvs分享了自己在Reddit上因发表讽刺言论而被永久封禁的经历，这引发了对言论自由和平台内容审核的进一步讨论。

补充讨论：
• Meta平台的账户封禁和申诉机制问题引发了广泛的关注和不满，用户认为缺乏透明和有效的申诉渠道。
• 对数字服务（如Instagram菜单、数字餐厅卡）的过度依赖引发了对用户设备要求和可访问性的争议。
• 用户对通过法律途径解决数字平台问题的有效性存在不同看法，一些人认为法律手段是必要的，而另一些人则认为这过于复杂和困难。
• 平台内容审核和用户举报机制的有效性和公正性受到质疑，用户认为平台在处理举报和封禁时缺乏充分的证据和透明的流程。

争议焦点：
• Meta平台账户封禁的合理性和申诉机制的缺失是主要争议点，用户对被封禁后缺乏有效的救济途径表示强烈不满。
• 数字服务过度依赖智能设备和互联网接入，忽视了用户多样化的需求和情况，这在用户中引发了对“数字化狂热”的批评。
• 平台内容审核和用户举报机制的公正性和有效性受到广泛质疑，用户认为当前机制存在明显缺陷，容易被滥用。

Background by
@matt__feeney
The dark side of account bans
Posted on
May 7, 2025
by
Maddy Miller
In
Technology
with tags
Accessibility
,
Retrospective
In the modern world, online accounts are ubiquitous. You’ve likely got so many that you’d have trouble actually counting them. Almost everything you do requires an account at this point. This wasn’t something I put too much thought into, beyond the mild annoyance of having to sign up to yet another website, until I was recently locked out of all Meta services for nearly two months. This experience was eye opening; it shocked me at how fundamental online platforms owned by companies have actually become to modern life.
What happened
For some background context, I develop a few Minecraft mods that are reasonably popular. If you’re not familiar with game modding communities,
they can be quite toxic sometimes
, with mod developers facing
significant harassment from certain users
. Because we were waiting for mod platforms to stabilise before publishing a final release of
WorldEdit
for a recently released Minecraft update, opting to only publish development builds until we were confident that it wouldn’t suddenly break, I received an anonymous threat.
Threat from an angry user
As threatened, this person attempted to get my online accounts banned. I’m not sure how many they reported, but a few hours later I was notified that my Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp accounts were all permanently banned. I was informed that I would not be able to create a new account, and to never attempt to gain access to a Meta-related system again. These kinds of threats were not new to me; I get hundreds a month. This was also not the first time I lost an account due to an angry user; I lost my PayPal account a few years ago and had to make a new one, due to a similar incident.
I got absolutely nowhere with support. I even paid for my partner’s account to access paid support, in an attempt to get in contact with a real person. I did end up speaking to a few engineers at Meta through connections, either directly or through others, many of which recommended suing Meta to unlock my accounts. This was extra complicated due to me living in Australia, so it’s not something I tried. Eventually, I decided to
make a tweet about it
. Despite the armies of spam bots that immediately inundated my notifications, eventually someone with the ability to unban accounts saw the tweet and unbanned me. The only way I managed to get my account back was sheer luck, likely heavily assisted by the number of people with large follower counts who retweeted my post. If I was not as connected as I am online, I likely would’ve been entirely out of luck.
The dark side of account bans
Now you might be thinking, “Maddy, losing a Facebook account isn’t the end of the world, right?” And yes, that’s what I thought too. I’d always wanted to reduce my reliance on Facebook, and I initially took this as a good excuse to. I was not at all anticipating how hard it would be.
Communication
Facebook is a social network, so the most obvious issue you’d face is losing contact with people on the platform. In Australia, a vast majority of people purely use Facebook Messenger as the way to keep in touch with people. While I’m not happy about it, that’s the current reality of Australian culture. My understanding is that it’s a similar situation with WhatsApp and most of Europe. This meant that not only did I immediately lose access to all of the group chats I was in, I lost my ability to actually contact many people. I don’t save people’s numbers in my contacts because I have everyone on Facebook Messenger, and I never call my friends on the phone.
When I did find alternative ways to contact people, or had other people do it for me, I was met with “Oh I don’t text, do you have Insta or WhatsApp?” If you haven’t noticed the pattern there, both of those platforms are owned by Meta. In Australia, Meta have a near monopoly on the concept of online communication.
Aspects of daily life
A few weeks into my “WorldEdit user”-ordered Meta detox, I tried to organise brunch with a friend. She recommended a few cafes, and I went to look at their menus. To my surprise, I couldn’t access their menus. They were only on Instagram, and it’d force a sign in before showing me the content. This was, of course, concerning. I hadn’t thought much about it beforehand, but so many restaurants and cafes here purely use Instagram (or sometimes Facebook) to host their menus, public holiday trading hours, or other important announcements.
I then went to sell some old PC hardware and asked around for a good marketplace to use. eBay had completely unreasonable fees, and the other ones used in Australia just didn’t have the right demographic to make that sort of sale. If I wanted to successfu

  - 一些评论者认为，自动化和AI将导致大量工作岗位的流失，特别是在制造业和服务业，这会加剧社会不平等。
  - 另一方则认为技术进步会创造新的就业机会，特别是在科技行业本身，且提高的生产力最终会使社会整体受益。

• 观点三：对先前讨论的引用和扩展
  - 部分评论者引用了之前讨论中的观点，认为需要对技术的影响进行更深入的分析和持续的讨论，以便更好地理解其长远效应。
  - 有人提出，先前的讨论缺乏对伦理问题的关注，建议在未来的讨论中增加对伦理和道德影响的考量。

补充讨论：
• 关于技术发展速度的问题
  - 一些评论者对技术发展的速度表示担忧，认为过快的技术进步可能导致社会、法律和伦理框架无法及时适应。

• 争议的焦点
  - 主要争议在于技术带来的利益和风险之间的平衡，特别是如何在推动技术进步的同时，尽量减少其负面影响，如失业、隐私问题和伦理困境。
  - 另一个焦点是关于社会对技术发展的准备程度，包括法律法规、教育体系和社会保障制度的适应能力。

总结来看，评论中的讨论围绕技术进步的潜力和风险展开，涉及技术对就业、社会问题的影响以及先前讨论的延续和扩展。争议主要集中在技术发展的利弊权衡和社会适应能力上。

data.title: ALICE detects the conversion of lead into gold at the LHC
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: ALICE合作组在《Physical Review C》发表论文，报告了在大型强子对撞机（LHC）中通过近距未碰撞的铅核产生的电磁相互作用，成功测量了铅转化为金的机制。这一现象类似于中世纪炼金术士梦寐以求的“点金术”。在LHC中，高能铅核产生的强电磁场引发光子与核的相互作用，导致核内部结构振荡，最终排出少量质子和中子，将铅（82个质子）转化为金（79个质子）。研究使用ALICE探测器的零度量能器（ZDC）检测了这一过程，发现LHC当前每秒可产生约89,000个金原子核，但其存在时间极短。在LHC第二轮运行期间，共产生了约860亿个金核，质量约为29皮克。随着LHC亮度的不断提升，第三轮运行产生的金量几乎是第二轮的两倍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型强子对撞机（LHC）通过实验从铅中生成金，但其商业可行性受到质疑。

不同观点：
• 观点一（成就令人印象深刻）：rubzah认为，LHC在三年内通过实验生成了29皮克的金，尽管每个金原子只存在几纳秒，这仍然是一个非常有趣且令人印象深刻的科学成就。

• 观点二（商业可行性不足）：rubzah指出，尽管实验生成了金，但由于每个金原子存在时间极短，尚不具备商业价值。换句话说，这一科学成果目前无法转化为实际的经济利益。

补充讨论：
• 科学价值 vs. 商业价值：评论暗示了科学实验的成果与其实际应用之间的差距。科学上生成金是一个值得注意的成就，但从商业角度来看，生成金的存在时间太短，无法形成有效的商业应用。

• 时间与稳定性问题：生成的金原子仅存在几纳秒，这意味着在当前技术条件下，无法积累足够稳定数量的金以满足任何商业需求，这也是其商业可行性受到质疑的原因。

争议焦点：
• 科学成就与实际应用之间的矛盾：虽然科学实验取得了进展，但其实际应用和商业价值仍存在较大疑问，这是评论中隐含的争议点。

ALICE detects the conversion of lead into gold at the Large Hadron Collider
by
CERN
ALICE detector. Credit: CERN
In a paper
published
in
Physical Review C
, the ALICE collaboration reports measurements that quantify the transmutation of lead into gold in CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
Transforming the base metal lead into the precious metal gold was a dream of medieval alchemists. This long-standing quest, known as chrysopoeia, may have been motivated by the observation that dull gray, relatively abundant lead is of a similar density to gold, which has long been coveted for its beautiful color and rarity. It was only much later that it became clear that lead and gold are distinct chemical elements and that chemical methods are powerless to transmute one into the other.
With the dawn of nuclear physics in the 20th century, it was discovered that
heavy elements
could transform into others—either naturally, by radioactive decay—or in the laboratory, under a bombardment of neutrons or protons. Though gold has been artificially produced in this way before, the ALICE collaboration has now measured the transmutation of lead into gold by a new mechanism involving near-miss collisions between
lead nuclei
at the LHC.
Extremely high-energy collisions between lead nuclei at the LHC can create quark–gluon plasma, a hot and dense state of matter that is thought to have filled the universe around a millionth of a second after the Big Bang, giving rise to the matter we now know. However, in the far more frequent interactions where the nuclei just miss each other without "touching," the intense electromagnetic fields surrounding them can induce photon–photon and photon–nucleus interactions that open further avenues of exploration.
The electromagnetic field emanating from a lead nucleus is particularly strong because the nucleus contains 82 protons, each carrying one elementary charge. Moreover, the very high speed at which lead nuclei travel in the LHC (corresponding to 99.999993% of the speed of light) causes the
electromagnetic field
lines to be squashed into a thin pancake, transverse to the direction of motion, producing a short-lived pulse of photons.
Often, this triggers a process called electromagnetic dissociation, whereby a photon interacting with a nucleus can excite oscillations of its internal structure, resulting in the ejection of small numbers of neutrons and protons. To create gold (a nucleus containing 79 protons), three protons must be removed from a lead nucleus in the LHC beams.
An ultra-peripheral collision where the two lead (
208
Pb) ion beams at the LHC pass by close to each other without colliding. In the electromagnetic dissociation process, a photon interacting with a nucleus can excite oscillations of its internal structure and result in the ejection of small numbers of neutrons (two) and protons (three), leaving the gold (
203
Au) nucleus behind. Credit: CERN
"It is impressive to see that our detectors can handle head-on collisions producing thousands of particles, while also being sensitive to collisions where only a few particles are produced at a time, enabling the study of rare electromagnetic 'nuclear transmutation' processes," says Marco Van Leeuwen, ALICE spokesperson.
The ALICE team used the detector's zero degree calorimeters (ZDC) to count the number of photon–nucleus interactions that resulted in the emission of zero, one, two and three protons accompanied by at least one neutron, which are associated with the production of lead, thallium, mercury and gold, respectively.

While less frequent than the creation of thallium or mercury, the results show that the LHC currently produces gold at a maximum rate of about 89,000 nuclei per second from lead–lead collisions at the ALICE collision point. Gold nuclei emerge from the collision with very high energy and hit the LHC beam pipe or collimators at various points downstream, where they immediately fragment into single protons, neutrons and other particles. The gold exists for just a tiny fraction of a second.
The ALICE analysis shows that, during Run 2 of the LHC (2015–2018), about 86 billion gold nuclei were created during the four major experiments. In terms of mass, this corresponds to just 29 picograms (2.9 × 10
-11

data.title: Senate passes "cruel" Republican plan to block Wi-Fi hotspots for schoolkids
data.author: croes
data.article_summary: 美国参议院今日投票决定废除联邦通信委员会（FCC）一项向学童提供Wi-Fi热点的计划。该计划旨在通过扩展E-Rate项目帮助没有可靠互联网 access 的学生完成作业。共和党支持者如参议员特德·克鲁兹（Ted Cruz）认为该计划可能让家长失去对孩子上网内容的控制，并可能导致对保守观点的审查。民主党则批评此举短视且残酷，将扩大数字鸿沟，阻碍学生获得必要资源。该计划若要正式废除，还需众议院通过并由总统特朗普签署。FCC主席布兰登·卡尔（Brendan Carr）此前曾反对该计划，认为只有国会能决定是否恢复。

The US Senate today voted along party lines to kill a Federal Communications Commission program to distribute Wi-Fi hotspots to schoolchildren, with Democrats saying the Republican-led vote will make it harder for kids without reliable Internet access to complete their homework.
The Senate approved a Congressional Review Act (CRA)
resolution
to nullify the hotspot rule, which was issued by the Federal Communications Commission
in July 2024
under then-Chairwoman Jessica Rosenworcel. The program would be eliminated if the
House version
passes and President Trump signs the joint resolution of disapproval.
Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas)
announced
the plan in January, saying the FCC program would "imped[e] parents' ability to decide what their kids see by subsidizing unsupervised access to inappropriate content." He also alleged that the hotspot program would shift control of Internet access from parents to schools and thus "heightens the risk of censoring kids' exposure to conservative viewpoints."
The Rosenworcel FCC's rule expanded E-Rate, a Universal Service Fund program,
allowing
schools and libraries to use E-Rate funding to lend out Wi-Fi hotspots and services that could be used off-premises. The FCC rule was titled, "Addressing the Homework Gap through the E-Rate Program," and the hotspot lending program was
scheduled to begin
in funding year 2025, which
starts in July 2025
.
Markey: “Cruel and shortsighted decision”
Today's Senate vote on the resolution of disapproval was 50–38. There was a 53–47
vote on Tuesday
that allowed the Senate measure to proceed to the final step. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.)
said on Tuesday
that "this resolution would prevent millions of students, educators, and families from getting online."
"It would be a disgrace if we deprive those students and their families of this vast resource, of literally life-changing access to a really necessary service that helps them not just now but throughout their futures," Blumenthal said. "We ought to expand Internet access, not constrict it. We ought to be enhancing it, not cutting it off."
Blumenthal pointed out that under a joint resolution of disapproval, the FCC is forbidden to adopt a similar rule in the future. "I have to ask, really? Are schools and teachers crying out to repeal this rule? Really? No, they are not. How does this proposal make any sense for them or for families? For the parents? For the community? It makes no sense," Blumenthal said.
Sen. Edward Markey (D-Mass.)
called
the Republican move "a cruel and shortsighted decision that will widen the digital divide and rob kids of the tools they need to succeed."
FCC’s new chair opposed lending program
The FCC previously distributed Wi-Fi hotspots and other Internet access technology through the Emergency Connectivity Fund (ECF) that was authorized by Congress in 2021. After that program was axed last year, the FCC responded by adapting E-Rate to include hotspot lending.
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, who was elevated to the agency's top spot by Trump in January, voted against the program last year. Carr said in his
dissent
that only Congress could decide whether to revive the hotspot lending.
"Now that the ECF program has expired, its future is up to Congress," he said at the time. "The legislative branch retains the power to decide whether to continue funding this Wi-Fi loaner program—or not. But Congress has made clear that the FCC's authority to fund this initiative is over."
Overall E-Rate funding is based on demand and
capped
at $4.94 billion per year. Actual spending for E-Rate in 2023 was
$2.48 billion
. E-Rate and other Universal Service Fund programs are paid for through fees imposed on phone companies, which generally pass the cost on to consumers.
The House version of the measure to kill the lending program was introduced by Rep. Russ Fulcher (R-Idaho). "E-Rate was designed to ensure schools and libraries have the connectivity they need to educate and serve their communities, not to create a backdoor entitlement program that stretches beyond the law's clear boundaries," Fulcher
said in February
when he filed the resolution. "The FCC cannot be allowed to unilaterally interpret the law in a way that fits their political agenda. The expansion of this program under the Biden administration was a blatant example of overreach that is not only unlawful but also disregards congressional intent."

data.title: Data manipulations alleged in study that paved way for Microsoft's quantum chip
data.author: EvgeniyZh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子计算研究的现状及其实际进展，特别是在微软相关研究中的数据操纵问题及其对整个领域的影响。

不同观点：
• **_heimdall**：认为量子计算研究像是烟雾弹，充斥着理论数学和未验证的奇迹主张，怀疑未来还会有更多数据操纵问题曝光。
• **krastanov**：对量子计算中的自然错误修正理论持积极看法，但感到失望和疲惫，因为该子领域存在大量数据操纵问题，对年轻科学家产生负面影响。
• **teekert**：引用Sabine的怀疑态度，指出微软在量子计算研究中的夸大问题，并提供相关文章链接。
• **Panoramix**：认为选择性使用数据不一定是决定性问题，但未披露则不妥。同时指出实验设备的制造难度和潜在的数据操纵迹象，但对研究结果不完全否定。
• **sschueller**：批评一些科研人员只是假装在做科学工作，而不是真正进行研究。
• **chermi**：反对因为微软的数据问题而全盘否定整个量子计算领域，强调该领域的稳步进展及研究难度，指出不同研究团队采用不同赌注式的研究路径。
• **os2warpman**：质疑量子计算发展多年仅消耗大量资源，而没有实质性成果，相比之下，核聚变研究至少产生了实用技术。

补充讨论：
• **russianGuy83829** 和 **trentnix**：以幽默方式评论事件，未提供实质性观点。
• **christkv** 和 **anonym29**：讽刺微软的研究成果，暗示其无实际价值。

争议焦点：
• 微软在量子计算研究中的数据操纵问题是否严重到足以质疑整个领域的进展。
• 量子计算领域是否在实际应用上进展缓慢，且消耗过多资源。
• 年轻科学家在数据操纵事件中的角色和受到的影响。
• 是否应因为个别公司的数据问题而全盘否定量子计算的潜在价值和进展。

data.title: Implementing a Struct of Arrays
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用C++26的反射机制实现一个结构体数组（Struct of Arrays, SoA），以替代传统的数组 of 结构体（Array of Structs, AoS）模式，从而提高内存使用效率和性能。文章借鉴了Andrew Kelley在Zig编译器中的优化思路，将原本组合在一起的结构体成员拆分为独立的数组存储。

文章首先解释了Zig语言中如何通过简单的代码修改实现这一优化，然后转向C++26，利用其反射特性来实现类似的`SoaVector<T>`。通过`std::meta::define_aggregate()`函数，文章展示了如何动态生成包含每个非静态数据成员指针的聚合结构体。接着，文章讨论了如何实现`push_back`和`grow`函数来管理动态数组，并确保每个数据成员数组同步增长。

文章的核心在于利用C++26的反射功能简化SoA模式的实现，避免手动处理每个成员的独立数组操作，同时提高代码的可维护性和性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++现代特性、Struct of Arrays (SoA) 实现及其在不同编程语言中的表现

不同观点：
• Perihelions 分享了如何在Common Lisp中实现SoA，提供了代码示例，展示了在不同语言中的实现方式。
• PessimalDecimal 认为文章最初像是对列式存储格式效率的讨论，但实际上展示了C++的臃肿和复杂性。
• Gr4vityWall 提到文章展示了现代C++的复杂性，并引用了Haxe宏的例子，同时质疑编译时类型生成宏的可读性问题。
• Monkeyelite 联想到“元对象协议的艺术”，提出在类定义和实现之间增加一个阶段来选择布局和访问方法。
• TheHideout 简单地将文章总结为结合面向对象编程（OOP）和实体组件系统（ECS）的优点。
• Sph 对文章中的特定语法（如^^type运算符）表示困惑，并寻求解释。
• The__alchemist 对比了Rust和Zig中的SoA实现，指出在数值和科学计算中的优势，并对文章中的抽象表示困惑。
• Gpderetta 提供了一个模板化的SoA实现示例，并质疑文章中反射的使用是否有显著优势。
• Mac3n 提到JOVIAL语言中的TABLE结构，引用了历史文档，展示了类似概念的早期实现。
• Jayd16 认为文章的核心是反射，并指出直接访问字段的假设是文章中一个荒谬但有趣的部分。
• Enthouan 认为文章内容在C语言中会更简单，对现代C++的复杂性表示不满。

补充讨论：
• 文章中反射的使用及其优势是争议焦点之一，部分评论者对其复杂性表示质疑。
• 不同编程语言（如Common Lisp、Haxe、Rust、Zig、C++等）中SoA实现的比较和优劣是另一个讨论热点。
• 一些评论者关注SoA实现中的可读性和抽象层次，特别是编译时类型生成和宏的使用。
• 历史语言（如JOVIAL）中类似概念的引用为讨论提供了一个历史视角。

data.title: Amazon's Vulcan Robots Now Stow Items Faster Than Humans
data.author: Luc
data.article_summary: 亚马逊的Vulcan机器人如今在存放物品速度上已超过人类。该公司一直在德国的一个仓库中测试这些机器人。与大多数专注于从箱子中拣选物品的仓库机器人不同，亚马逊的Vulcan机器人解决了将物品存入箱子的不同挑战。这一进展标志着仓储自动化技术的又一重要里程碑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自动化和机器人在物流和仓储领域的应用及其社会影响

不同观点：
• [thisisnotauser] 认为，随着自动化（如亚马逊仓库中的机器人）的推进，工人失业将导致消费能力下降，最终没有人购买产品。此观点关注自动化对消费市场的潜在负面影响。

• [philipwhiuk] 指出，亚马逊让机器人融入人类设计的仓库，而Ocado则是人类监督机器人仓库，认为后者是更容易解决的问题。此观点对比了不同公司在自动化应用上的策略差异。

• [omneity] 对仓库中出现带有可伸缩刀片的机器人表示惊讶，并分享了相关视频，关注自动化技术的新奇和潜在风险。

• [mapt] 认为尝试让机器完成类似于“长shoreman's Tetris”的任务是不必要的，建议采用标准集装箱化系统，该系统已经几乎完全取代了人工搬运工作。此观点质疑某些自动化应用的必要性。

• [londons_explore] 对仓库中50万次存货操作表示数量不大，认为人类完成这些操作的时间相对较短，暗示自动化在效率提升上的实际效果有限。

• [voidUpdate] 质疑“真正的触觉”的定义，提出过去是否已经有能够检测施加力的机器人，并怀疑那些是否是“假的触觉”。此观点探讨了技术术语和实际应用的准确性。

• [matthewfelgate] 关心公司是否在设计更适合机器人操作的产品包装，关注产品设计与自动化技术兼容性的问题。

• [m3kw9] 认为自动化减少低端工作岗位的同时，可能会创造新的工作机会，未来人们不应被迫从事低端工作。此观点对自动化持乐观态度，认为它可能带来社会进步。

• [LeonB] 引用了一个幽默的未来工厂描述，认为未来工厂只需要一个人和一只狗，人喂狗，狗看护设备。此观点以幽默方式表达了对高度自动化的设想。

• [mensetmanusman] 对普通人类能否胜任仓储工作表示怀疑，暗示机器人可能比人类更有效率。

• [oxqbldpxo] 质疑未来是否会减少购买不必要的商品，关注自动化对消费文化的影响。

• [elzbardico] 担心在没有社会主义的情况下，自动化可能导致社会不平等加剧，技术寡头统治社会，社会流动性降低。此观点探讨了自动化对社会结构和民主的潜在威胁。

• [danielovichdk] 对AI替代人工的速度表示惊讶，认为某些自动化技术本应更早实现。此观点质疑自动化技术的发展速度和应用时机。

补充讨论：
- 自动化对就业市场和社会结构的潜在影响是讨论的焦点之一，不同观点对自动化带来的机会和风险有不同看法。
- 技术定义和实际应用的准确性也是讨论的重要内容，如“真正的触觉”和自动化效率的实际评估。
- 自动化对消费市场和消费文化的长远影响引起了关注，部分观点质疑自动化是否会导致消费能力下降或改变消费习惯。

data.title: How async/await works in Python
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要介绍了Python中的`async`和`await`关键字，以及它们如何使程序变得异步。文章指出，尽管`async`/`await`语法看似同步代码，但实际上允许程序在等待I/O等操作完成时执行其他任务。要理解其工作原理，需了解并发、并行、事件循环、I/O多路复用、异步、协程等概念。

文章强调，即便不使用特殊语言特性也可以编写并发程序，但`async`/`await`使并发编程更加便捷。文章通过构建一个TCP回显服务器，逐步展示从顺序执行到并发版本的演变过程，包括使用OS线程和单线程I/O多路复用与事件循环的方法，最终引入生成器、协程及`async`/`await`。

文章从最简单的顺序服务器代码开始，逐步改进以处理多个客户端，并解释了每个步骤的核心概念和实现方法。

Mark functions as
async
. Call them with
await
. All of a sudden, your program becomes asynchronous – it can do useful things while it waits for other things, such as I/O operations, to complete.
Code written in the
async
/
await
style looks like regular synchronous code but works very differently. To understand how it works, one should be familiar with many non-trivial concepts including concurrency, parallelism, event loops, I/O multiplexing, asynchrony, cooperative multitasking and coroutines. Python's implementation of
async
/
await
adds even more concepts to this list: generators, generator-based coroutines, native coroutines,
yield
and
yield from
. Because of this complexity, many Python programmers that use
async
/
await
do not realize how it actually works. I believe that it should not be the case. The
async
/
await
pattern can be explained in a simple manner if you start from the ground up. And that's what we're going to do today.
Note
: In this post I'm referring to CPython 3.9. Some implementation details will certainly change as CPython evolves. I'll try to keep track of important changes and add update notes.
It's all about concurrency
Computers execute programs sequentially – one instruction after another. But a typical program performs multiple tasks, and it doesn't always make sense to wait for some task to complete before starting the next one. For example, a chess program that waits for a player to make a move should be able to update the clock in the meantime. Such an ability of a program to deal with multiple things simultaneously is what we call
concurrency
. Concurrency doesn't mean that multiple tasks must run at the same physical time. They can run in an interleaved manner: a task runs for some time, then suspends and lets other tasks run, hoping it will get more time in the future. By this mechanism, an OS can run thousands of processes on a machine that has only a few cores. If multiple tasks do run at the same physical time, as in the case of a multi-core machine or a cluster, then we have
parallelism
, a special case of concurrency
[1]
.
It's crucial to realize that you can write concurrent programs without any special support from the language. Suppose you write a program that performs two tasks, each task being represented by a separate function:

do_task1
():
# ...

do_task2
():
# ...

main
():
do_task1
()
do_task2
()
If the tasks are independent, then you can make the program concurrent by decomposing each function into several functions and call the decomposed functions in an interleaved manner, like so:

():
# ...
def
do_task1_part2
():
# ...
def
do_task2_part1
():
# ...
def
do_task2_part2
():
# ...
def
main
():
do_task1_part1
()
do_task2_part1
()
do_task1_part2
()
do_task2_part2
()
Of course, this is an oversimplified example. The point here is that the language doesn't determine whether you can write concurrent programs or not but may provide features that make concurrent programming more convenient. As we'll learn today,
async
/
await
is just such a feature.
To see how one goes from concurrency to
async
/
await
, we'll write a real-world concurrent program – a TCP echo server that supposed to handle multiple clients simultaneously. We'll start with the simplest, sequential version of the server that is not concurrent. Then we'll make it concurrent using OS threads. After that, we'll see how we can write a concurrent version that runs in a single thread using I/O multiplexing and an event loop. From this point onwards, we'll develop the single-threaded approach by introducing generators, coroutines and, finally,
async
/
await
.
A sequential server
Writing a TCP echo server that handles only one client at a time is straightforward. The server listens for incoming connections on some port, and when a client connects, the server talks to the client until the connection is closed. Then it continues to listen for new connections. The Catholic Church has issued a warning to its clergy in Washington state: Any priest who complies with a new law requiring the reporting of child abuse confessions to authorities will be excommunicated.
The new law, which will take effect on July 27, eliminates the long-standing confidentiality of the confessional, forcing Catholic leaders and lawmakers into a highly charged standoff over religious liberty and child protection.
However, the Archdiocese of Seattle and several bishops argue that the law not only contravenes church doctrine but crosses constitutional lines, while supporters maintain it is a crucial step to protect minors from abuse.
Newsweek
contacted the Archdiocese of Seattle and Washington Governor Bob Ferguson and the three Democratic state senators who sponsored the bill for comment via email and online inquiry forms.
The sun rises behind a stone cross atop the historic Cathedral Basilica of St. Frances of Assisi in Santa Fe, New Mexico.
The sun rises behind a stone cross atop the historic Cathedral Basilica of St. Frances of Assisi in Santa Fe, New Mexico.
Robert Alexander/GETTY
Why It Matters
The issue spotlights the enduring tension between religious freedom and the state's duty to protect children from abuse. By compelling clergy to breach the confessional seal, Washington joins a small group of states stripping traditional confidentiality protections.
The law has triggered a national conversation about the boundaries of church and state, setting a precedent that could have implications for religious practices and privileged communications nationwide. The outcome may influence how other states approach mandated reporting requirements for clergy, especially as constitutional and civil rights groups enter the debate.
What To Know
Washington's new statute requires clergy to report suspected child abuse, explicitly denying exceptions for information revealed during confession.
"Catholic clergy may not violate the seal of confession—or they will be excommunicated from the Church," the Archdiocese of Seattle warned, according to
Fox News
.
The Catholic Church's canon law regards breaking the confessional seal as a grave offense: "A confessor who directly violates the seal of confession incurs an automatic excommunication reserved to the Apostolic See."
The U.S.
Department of Justice
said it is investigating whether the law infringes on First Amendment religious protections.

data.title: Malaya's Timeless Design
data.author: cenazoic
data.article_summary: 本文是一份关于椰子行动党（Coconut Action Party）的详细研究，涵盖了多个方面的内容。文章讨论了椰子主题邮票的设计、印制及其演变历史，包括手刻字体、雕刻周期和印刷技术等。它还深入分析了邮票的纸张、水印、颜色和油墨，以及伪造邮票和印花税票的问题。地理上，文章涉及了全球各地的椰子设计，如马来西亚各州、新加坡和荷属东印度等地。此外，文章探讨了邮票的防伪标志、版号和一些历史事件，如二战对邮票的影响。技术方面，文章运用了多种科学方法分析邮票，如表面形貌分析、纤维分析和光谱学等。最后，文章附有参考文献和附录，提供了详细的椰子主题邮票目录和百科全书。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕邮票及其相关话题的讨论，包括个人经历、技术细节以及对人生意义的哲学思考。

不同观点：
• [kubb] 认为人们能够在看似平凡的事物中找到深刻的意义，并提出如果人们不再需要工作，他们依然能够通过创造意义来找到生活的充实感。这种观点强调了人类寻找和创造意义的能力，并设想在一个没有工作需求的世界里，人们可能会探索出我们目前无法想象的新知识领域。

• [weiliddat] 分享了个人与邮票相关的家庭历史和文化背景，特别是马来西亚和新加坡的后殖民时期。他提到父亲在殖民时期的教育经历以及自己参与邮票收集活动的童年回忆。这代表了一种对邮票的情感和文化传承的观点，强调了邮票在特定历史背景下的个人和文化意义。

• [KaiserPro] 更关注技术细节，特别是网站上使用的字体效果。他注意到字体的微小动态变化，并讨论了这种效果是字体设计的一部分还是渲染过程中的产物。这代表了一种从技术角度看待邮票及其展示方式的观点。

• [ayushrodrigues] 简单地表达了对邮票超越时间的特质的欣赏，认为很难从邮票中判断其具体的时代背景。这是一种对邮票设计和艺术价值的审美评价。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[kubb] 对人生意义的哲学思考与其他评论对邮票历史和技术的具体讨论形成对比，但没有直接的争议。
• 历史与文化传承：[weiliddat] 的评论提供了邮票在特定历史和文化背景下的个人视角，补充了 [kubb] 对邮票普遍意义的抽象思考。
• 技术细节：[KaiserPro] 的评论引入了对字体技术的关注，这是其他评论中未涉及的方面，显示了讨论的多样性。
• 审美评价：[ayushrodrigues] 的评论简洁地总结了邮票的艺术和时间无关的特性，与其他评论形成互补。

data.title: How "Night of the Living Dead" Accidentally Became Public Domain
data.author: edavis
data.article_summary: 《活死人之夜》是由乔治·罗梅罗执导的经典恐怖片，奠定了现代僵尸的形象：无智力的行尸走肉，渴望活人 flesh。该片因发行商忘记添加版权声明而进入公共领域，导致罗梅罗损失了数百万潜在收入。尽管如此，影片因其易得性而成为经典，影响了如《行尸走肉》和《僵尸之地》等众多作品。罗梅罗后续拍摄了五部僵尸电影，其中《活死人黎明》被认为是最出色的续作。尽管他在好莱坞未获足够认可，但罗梅罗作为僵尸电影教父的地位无可撼动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕电影《Night of the Living Dead》版权问题及其影响的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• [teddyh] 认为，电影《Night of the Living Dead》由于版权问题导致了经济损失，并提到这种现象类似于“如果Linus Torvalds对Linux收费，他今天会很有钱”的情况。然而，他也指出，这部电影因其免费提供的性质而成为经典，因为易于访问和频繁的电视播放让更多人看到了这部电影。

• [另一观点 - teddyh 继续] 认为，电影成为经典是完全意料之中的，如果它只是一部受版权保护的老黑白电影，今天它可能只是一个历史注脚。

• [nico] 指出，版权的持续时间过长（作者一生加去世后70年），认为这一点很荒谬。

• [gus_massa] 提供了法律背景，指出电影发行时（1968年）的版权法与现在的不同。他解释了1989年前后版权声明要求的差异，并提到如果作品在特定时间段内没有采取纠正措施，可能会失去版权保护。

• [Malic] 提到了类似的案例，1963年的电影《Charade》也发生了同样的版权问题，进入了公有领域。

• [wodenokoto] 质疑发行方是否真的拥有足够的电影所有权来发布修改版进入公有领域。他还提到一个类似案例，一个语言学习初创公司smart.fm在RSS上发布了他们的材料在左版许可下，但他们并没有有意放弃这些材料，也没有权利重新许可这些材料。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了版权法历史和变化，以及具体案例如《Night of the Living Dead》和《Charade》如何受到影响。
• 探讨了版权问题对作品传播和经典地位的影响。

43909179.article_content:
George Romero's
Night of the Living Dead
is one of the most popular horror films ever, but an unfortunate error accidentally made it public domain. With
Night of the Living Dead,
Romero created the zombie
as we know it today, a walking corpse with little intelligence that craves the flesh of the living. Without
Night of the Living Dead,
there would be no
The Walking Dead,
Zombieland,
or hundreds of other zombie movies and TV shows. When it comes to zombies, Romero is the godfather.
Romero would of course go on to direct five other zombie films, although most had no explicit connection to each other. Many would argue his greatest was
Night
's sequel,
Dawn of the Dead,
although
Day of the Dead
also has its diehard fans. While Romero might've preferred he not just be known as the guy who makes zombie movies, most of them are so good it's easy to see why he's so closely identified with the sub-genre.
Related:
10 Best Horror Movies Of The 1960s
Unfortunately, despite
Night of the Living Dead
's massive success, Romero never really got the respect from Hollywood he truly deserved, if only because his independent spirit made him reluctant to compromise his creative visions to fit studio mandates. Romero also never achieved the massive fortune he rightfully earned by co-writing and directing
Night of the Living Dead,
due to a ridiculous error by the film's initial distributor.
Night of the Living Dead's Distributor Forgot to Copyright the Film
Night of the Living Dead
today exists within the
public domain,
meaning copies of the film are free to watch and share. That's why the film has had dozens of home video releases by different companies, as all they had to do is acquire a copy of the film, and then they could freely release it without cutting any kind of deal with Romero or his collaborators.
Night of the Living Dead
being public domain is the fault of the film's distributor, who didn't put the required copyright notice on the theatrical prints. This error occurred after the film's title was changed from its original moniker
Night of the Flesh Eaters.
Prints with that title contained the copyright notice, but when new prints were created using the title
Night of the Living Dead,
the copyright notice was forgotten.
Night of the Living Dead Being Public Domain Cost George Romero Millions
As the late, great
George Romero
lamented publicly on more than one occasion,
Night of the Living Dead
's copyright snafu ended up costing him untold amounts of money in both the short and long term.
Night of the Living Dead
made over $30 million at the box office, a massive sum for the late 1960s that Romero saw little of. Romero also didn't make any money off of most of the aforementioned home video releases, outside of some by more reputable companies that saw fit to involve Romero in their products.
Night of the Living Dead
also saw multiple theatrical re-releases. Somewhat ironically though, it's
Night of the Living Dead
's freely available nature that helped it become the revered classic it is today, as easy access and constant TV airings ensured that more and more people saw the film.

data.title: The Linux Kernel's PGP Web of Trust
data.author: JNRowe
data.article_summary: Linux内核开发过程中使用PGP签名，主线维护者需在提交给Linus Torvalds的拉取请求中使用签名标签。由于密钥服务器概念存在问题，Konstantin Ryabitsev通过一个Git仓库维护相关密钥，目前有602个有效密钥。要加入该仓库，密钥需在5步信任路径内与Linus的密钥相连。当前有2个密钥因信任路径丢失受影响。GnuPG 2.4.x开始拒绝使用SHA-1算法的第三方签名，尽管这暂时不影响内核PGP密钥库，因为信任路径检查不依赖GnuPG的签名信任。然而，若全部SHA-1签名被弃用，将有大量密钥失去信任路径，包括多位知名内核开发者的密钥。为改善此问题，将在Embedded Recipes 2025会议期间举办密钥签名活动，参与者需在2025年5月12日前提交公钥。
data.comments_summary:

43935356.article_content:
The Linux kernel's development process makes use of PGP. The most relevant part
here is that subsystem maintainers are supposed to use signed tags in their
pull requests to Linus Torvalds. As the concept of keyservers is
considered
broken
,
Konstantin Ryabitsev maintains a collection of relevant keys in a
git
repository
.
As of today (at commit
a0bc65fb27f5033beddf9d1ad97d67c353849be2
)
there are 602 valid keys tracked in that repository. The requirement for a key
to be added there is that there must be at least one trust path from Linus
Torvalds' key to this key of length at most 5 within that keyring.
Occasionally it happens that a key loses its trust paths because someone in
these paths replaced their key, or keys expired. Currently this affects 2 keys.
However there is a problem on the horizon: GnuPG 2.4.x started to reject
third-party key signatures using the SHA-1 hash algorithm. In general that's
good,
SHA-1 isn't considered secure any more since more than 20
years
.
This doesn't directly affect the kernel-pgpkeys repo, because the trust path
checking doesn't rely on GnuPG trusting the signatures; there is a dedicated
tool that parses the keyring contents and currently accepts signatures using
SHA-1. Also signatures are not thrown away usually, but there are exceptions:
Recently Theodore Ts'o
asked to update his
certificate
.
When Konstantin imported the updated certificate GnuPG's "cleaning" was applied
which dropped all SHA-1 signatures. So Theodore Ts'o's key lost 168 signatures,
among them one by Linus Torvalds on his primary UID.
That made me wonder what would be the effect on the web of trust if all SHA-1
signatures were dropped. Here are the facts:
There are 7976 signatures tracked in the korg-pgpkeys repo that are
considered valid, 6045 of them use SHA-1.
Only considering the primary UID Linus Torvalds directly signed 40 public
keys, 38 of these using SHA-1. One of the two keys that is still "properly"
signed, doesn't sign any other key. So nearly all trust paths go through a
single key.
When not considering SHA-1 signatures there are 485 public keys without a
trust path from Linus Torvalds of length 5 or less. So today these 485
public keys would not qualify to be added to the pgpkeys git repository.
Among the people being dropped are Andrew Morton, Greg Kroah-Hartman, H.
Peter Anvin, Ingo Molnar, Junio C Hamano, Konstantin Ryabitsev, Peter
Zijlstra, Stephen Rothwell and Thomas Gleixner.
The size of the kernel strong set is reduced from 358 to 94.
If you attend
Embedded Recipes 2025
next
week, there is an opportunity to improve the situation: Together with
Ahmad
Fatoum
I'm organizing a keysigning session. If
you want to participate, send your public key to
er2025-keysigning@baylibre.com
before
2025-05-12 08:00 UTC.
43935356.article_summary: Linux内核开发过程中使用PGP签名，主线维护者需在提交给Linus Torvalds的拉取请求中使用签名标签。由于密钥服务器概念存在问题，Konstantin Ryabitsev通过一个Git仓库维护相关密钥，目前有602个有效密钥。要加入该仓库，密钥需在5步信任路径内与Linus的密钥相连。当前有2个密钥因信任路径丢失受影响。GnuPG 2.4.x开始拒绝使用SHA-1算法的第三方签名，尽管这暂时不影响内核PGP密钥库，因为信任路径检查不依赖GnuPG的签名信任。然而，若全部SHA-1签名被弃用，将有大量密钥失去信任路径，包括多位知名内核开发者的密钥。为改善此问题，将在Embedded Recipes 2025会议期间举办密钥签名活动，参与者需在2025年5月12日前提交公钥。

data.title: No! Repent! From! Harlan! (1998)
data.author: Michelangelo11
data.article_summary: Harlan Ellison, a highly acclaimed science fiction writer, discusses his preference for using a manual typewriter over modern technology like computers. Despite the widespread adoption of digital tools in writing, Ellison values the tactile, direct connection he feels with his work on a typewriter. He criticizes the ease that computers offer, arguing that art should be difficult and that struggle contributes to the creative process. While acknowledging that some writers, like Connie Willis and Dan Simmons, succeed using computers, Ellison emphasizes his personal method and rejects the notion that technology necessarily improves artistic output. He urges others to respect his choice, just as he respects theirs.

43897816.article_content:
No! Repent! From! Harlan!
A fair review of Harlan Ellison's credentials would take more wordage than allowed for this entire interview. Rest assured he's only the world's most honored fantasist. A tiny sampling of the awards he's won: the Hugo (eight and a half times), Nebula (three times), Bram Stoker (three times), the Edgar (twice), and the Writers Guild of America Award (four times). Stanley Wiater recently discussed with Ellison the three latest of the 70-plus books he's published in a four-decade career:
Slippage
,
"Repent, Harlequin!" said the Ticktockman
, and the
Edgeworks
series. Given his never-stop schedule, one question per book seemed appropriate.
Amazon.com:
At the beginning of
Slippage
, your latest short story collection, you make the following declaration: "IT SHOULD BE NOTED: THE AUTHOR DOES NOT HAVE A COMPUTER. THE AUTHOR DOES NOT HAVE A MODEM. THE AUTHOR IS NOT ONLINE. THE AUTHOR WORKS ON A REAL, ACTUAL FINGER-DRIVEN MANUAL TYPEWRITER, NOT EVEN AN ELECTRIC ONE. THE AUTHOR IS NOT A LUDDITE, HE JUST PERCEIVES OF ALL THIS ELECTRONIC CRAP AS THE TWILIGHT OF THE WORD." Would you explain?
Harlan Ellison:
Seems glowingly clear to me. But, okay, it's very simply this. I am not a Luddite. I have a photocopier in my house. I have a fax machine. I keep my telephone numbers in a little portable 64K Rolodex. I have a modern car that I drive, but I also have a 1947 Packard. I also listen to
Glenn Miller
--when I'm not listening to
Stevie Ray Vaughan
. Bottom line: you should work at the level of technology that best does the job. Anything beyond that is nothing but toots and whistles guaranteed to do nothing more than put money in
Bill Gates's
pocket.
I have no need to work on a computer. I don't like working on a PC. I don't like having to "boot" something up; I don't like having to "format" something. I like being able to sit down, roll my paper into the platen, and begin boogeying! I'm
Captain Nemo
--I sit down at the pipe organ and I raise my hands and then I'm godlike and create "Toccata & Fugue in D Minor." I sit there and feel the crackling emergence of the art from my fingertips. I drink in the joy of being in direct sexual contact with the Muse. It's heady wine!
Listen: I work the way that best suits ME. I don't tell other people to work on typewriters; I don't go around proselytizing. But--the zombie pod-people who work on these machines come around and proselytize ME. As if I'm doing something [as a fellow writer] that demeans THEM, and makes THEM look bad. It's like when you're at a party, and you don't drink, and everybody else is completely bagged out of their mind, or vomiting on their shoes, and they keep trying to get YOU to drink. And you keep saying "No thank you. I don't want any." It's as if their paranoia drives them, by implication, to assume you're saying something negative about them. So they have to keep trying to make you one of their own.
It may not be magical [working on a typewriter], but it is unique. People say to me, "But the computer makes it easier." It shouldn't BE easier!! Art is not supposed to be "easier." Art is supposed to be harder. Commerce should be easy. Friendships should be easy. Good marriages should be easy. Driving a car should be easy. Getting laid should be easy. Art should be DIFFICULT. It's as
Faulkner
said when he was accepting the Nobel Prize: "It's the study of the human heart in conflict with itself, which is the only thing worth the blood and the anguish of writing." As the fabulous sportswriter
Red Smith
once said, "There's nothing to writing. All you do is sit down at a typewriter and open a vein."
I like the feel, I like the actual FEEL of sitting there and doing the physical labor. I think that it's good for an artist to sweat! I think it's good for an artist to have to struggle a little bit. Sometimes things that make it easier are good, but most times things that make it easier are only short cuts.
I started saying this when writers started using laptops years ago, and everybody rushed to convert, because everybody wants to keep up with the Joneses, or in this field, the
Bruce Sterlings
. And I warned them. "You're going to find that frighteningly soon all we're going to have here are
Star Wars
and
Star Trek
novels, and you're going to find that the quality of work you want to do is not going to be coming out of you."
There are of course people who work on computers who do very, very well.
Connie Willis
,
Jack McDevitt
,
Dan Simmons
, people like that do very well. But I think, for the majority of writers who need to have a connection to their work...creating on a typewriter or a pen and pad while sitting in a comfortable armchair is a far cooler way to get the job done gloriously. But I don't put down anyone else's way of doing it; they want to work on a PC? Fine! Let 'em work on a PC! Let 'em chisel it in onyx on the side of a mountain! Let 'em skywrite it with a crop-dusting biplane, for all I give a s--t. Just stop busting my chops,

data.title: WASM 2.0
data.author: lioeters
data.article_summary:
WebAssembly (Wasm) 是一种安全、可移植的低级代码格式，旨在高效执行和紧凑表示。其目标是实现高性能的网页应用，但不局限于网页，也可用于其他环境。Wasm 是一个开放标准，由 W3C 社区小组开发，本文档介绍了其 2.0 版的核心标准。

### 设计目标
- **快速、安全、便携**：接近原生性能，内存安全，防止数据损坏和安全漏洞。
- **硬件和语言无关**：支持多种现代架构和编程语言。
- **开放**：程序可以与其环境简单交互。
- **高效、可移植**：二进制格式紧凑，模块化，可流式和并行处理。

### 范围
WebAssembly 是一个虚拟指令集架构（virtual ISA），核心规范定义了指令集、二进制编码、验证和执行语义，但不包括与具体执行环境的交互。

### 安全考虑
WebAssembly 无法直接访问执行环境，所有交互需通过嵌入器提供的函数进行。嵌入器负责制定安全策略，可能需要应对侧信道攻击。

### 依赖
WebAssembly 依赖于 [IEEE-754-2019] 浮点数表示和 [UNICODE] 名称表示标准。

总结：WebAssembly 是一种跨平台、高效的代码格式，适用于多种环境，具有严格的安全和设计目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebAssembly (Wasm) 2.0 发布及其新特性讨论

不同观点：
• [lioeters] 认为 Wasm 2.0 引入了大量新特性，如向量指令、批量内存指令、多值返回、引用类型、非陷阱转换和符号扩展指令，显著增强了语言的功能，特别是在性能优化方面，如音视频编解码、机器学习和加密计算。
• [AlexAltea] 对 Wasm 2.0 的发布总体持积极态度，但失望于采用了固定大小的 SIMD（128位宽）而不是自适应宽度 SIMD，认为后者能更好地根据主机能力最大化 SIMD 宽度，类似于 ARM SVE 的工作方式。
• [Klasiaster] 指出 Wasm 和 WASI 目前缺乏动态实例化功能，即一个 Wasm 程序能够在运行时启动另一个 Wasm 程序，这是 Wasm 成为 POSIX 替代方案所真正欠缺的。
• [TekMol] 对 Wasm 的实用性持怀疑态度，认为 Wasm 带来的速度提升有限，编译到 JavaScript 也能实现同样的跨语言运行效果。
• [Dabbling_Dion] 认为 Wasm 没有直接的浏览器 DOM 访问支持，所有努力都是徒劳的，必须依赖 JavaScript "shim"。

补充讨论：
• [pdubroy] 提供了一个学习 Wasm 的资源，推荐通过构建一个简单编译器来学习 Wasm，并提供了在线书籍链接。
• [inoffensivename] 分享了对 Wasm 规范的积极体验，认为尽管入门难，但规范详尽且有参考解释器和测试，值得研究。
• [anentropic] 询问是否有运行时已经实现了 Wasm 2.0 的新特性。
• [BuckRogers] 以 C# 开发者角度表达了对 Wasm 2.0 的期待，特别是 Blazor 在 Wasm 上的应用。
• [rossant] 提出关于 C 函数返回结构体值能否编译为 Wasm 的问题。
• [iFire] 提到编写高级 Wasm 绑定时遇到非 int 或 float 类型的问题。
• [aleksi] 对 Editor's Draft 中的 "bikeshed" 出现在 URL 中感到好奇。
• [canadiantim] 提问 Wasm 是否比纯 JavaScript 更“安全”。

争议焦点：
• Wasm 2.0 引入的固定大小 SIMD 是否如自适应 SIMD 一样有效。
• Wasm 是否真正提供了足够的优势来替代 JavaScript 或其他现有技术。
• 直接浏览器支持和 DOM 访问对 Wasm 的重要性。

Introduction
WebAssembly (abbreviated Wasm
[

) is a
safe, portable, low-level code format
designed for efficient execution and compact representation.
Its main goal is to enable high performance applications on the Web, but it does not make any Web-specific assumptions or provide Web-specific features, so it can be employed in other environments as well.
WebAssembly is an open standard developed by a
W3C Community Group
.
This document describes version 2.0 (Draft 2024-12-18) of the
core
WebAssembly standard.
It is intended that it will be superseded by new incremental releases with additional features in the future.
1.1.1.
Design Goals
The design goals of WebAssembly are the following:
Fast, safe, and portable
semantics
:
Fast
: executes with near native code performance, taking advantage of capabilities common to all contemporary hardware.
Safe
: code is validated and executes in a memory-safe
[
2
]
, sandboxed environment preventing data corruption or security breaches.
Well-defined
: fully and precisely defines valid programs and their behavior in a way that is easy to reason about informally and formally.
Hardware-independent
: can be compiled on all modern architectures, desktop or mobile devices and embedded systems alike.
Language-independent
: does not privilege any particular language, programming model, or object model.
Platform-independent
: can be embedded in browsers, run as a stand-alone VM, or integrated in other environments.
Open
: programs can interoperate with their environment in a simple and universal manner.
Efficient and portable
representation
:
Compact
: has a binary format that is fast to transmit by being smaller than typical text or native code formats.
Modular
: programs can be split up in smaller parts that can be transmitted, cached, and consumed separately.
Efficient
: can be decoded, validated, and compiled in a fast single pass, equally with either just-in-time (JIT) or ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation.
Streamable
: allows decoding, validation, and compilation to begin as soon as possible, before all data has been seen.
Parallelizable
: allows decoding, validation, and compilation to be split into many independent parallel tasks.
Portable
: makes no architectural assumptions that are not broadly supported across modern hardware.
WebAssembly code is also intended to be easy to inspect and debug, especially in environments like web browsers, but such features are beyond the scope of this specification.
[
1
]
A contraction of “WebAssembly”, not an acronym, hence not using all-caps.
[
2
]
No program can break WebAssembly’s memory model. Of course, it cannot guarantee that an unsafe language compiling to WebAssembly does not corrupt its own memory layout, e.g. inside WebAssembly’s linear memory.
1.1.2.
Scope
At its core, WebAssembly is a
virtual instruction set architecture (virtual ISA)
.
As such, it has many use cases and can be embedded in many different environments.
To encompass their variety and enable maximum reuse, the WebAssembly specification is split and layered into several documents.
This document is concerned with the core ISA layer of WebAssembly.
It defines the instruction set, binary encoding, validation, and execution semantics, as well as a textual representation.
It does not, however, define how WebAssembly programs can interact with a specific environment they execute in, nor how they are invoked from such an environment.
Instead, this specification is complemented by additional documents defining interfaces to specific embedding environments such as the Web.
These will each define a WebAssembly
application programming interface (API)
suitable for a given environment.
1.1.3.
Security Considerations
WebAssembly provides no ambient access to the computing environment in which code is executed.
Any interaction with the environment, such as I/O, access to resources, or operating system calls, can only be performed by invoking
functions
provided by the
embedder
and imported into a WebAssembly
module
.
An embedder can establish security policies suitable for a respective environment by controlling or limiting which functional capabilities it makes available for import.
Such considerations are an embedder’s responsibility and the subject of
API definitions
for a specific environment.
Because WebAssembly is designed to be translated into machine code running directly on the host’s hardware, it is potentially vulnerable to side channel attacks on the hardware level.
In environments where this is a concern, an embedder may have to put suitable mitigations into place to isolate WebAssembly computations.
1.1.4.
Dependencies
WebAssembly depends on two existing standards:
[IEEE-754-2019]
, for the representation of
floating-point data
and the semantics of respective
numeric operations
.
[UNICODE]
, for the representation of import/export
names
and the
text format
.

43934711.article_summary:
WebAssembly (Wasm) 是一种安全、可移植的低级代码格式，旨在高效执行和紧凑表示。其目标是实现高性能的网页应用，但不局限于网页，也可用于其他环境。Wasm 是一个开放标准，由 W3C 社区小组开发，本文档介绍了其 2.0 版的核心标准。

### 设计目标
- **快速、安全、便携**：接近原生性能，内存安全，防止数据损坏和安全漏洞。
- **硬件和语言无关**：支持多种现代架构和编程语言。
- **开放**：程序可以与其环境简单交互。
- **高效、可移植**：二进制格式紧凑，模块化，可流式和并行处理。

### 范围
WebAssembly 是一个虚拟指令集架构（virtual ISA），核心规范定义了指令集、二进制编码、验证和执行语义，但不包括与具体执行环境的交互。

### 安全考虑
WebAssembly 无法直接访问执行环境，所有交互需通过嵌入器提供的函数进行。嵌入器负责制定安全策略，可能需要应对侧信道攻击。

### 依赖
WebAssembly 依赖于 [IEEE-754-2019] 浮点数表示和 [UNICODE] 名称表示标准。

总结：WebAssembly 是一种跨平台、高效的代码格式，适用于多种环境，具有严格的安全和设计目标。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Rack::Session::Pool中间件中的一个安全漏洞（CVE-2025-46336，GHSA-9j94-67jr-4cqj），该漏洞可能导致并发请求恢复已删除的会话，使未认证用户能够占用该会话。漏洞影响版本为rack-session < 2.0.0，已修复版本为>= 2.1.1。如果攻击者获取了会话 cookie，并能在用户登出时触发长时间请求，可能维持非法访问。建议更新至最新版本或通过原子化会话无效化等方法进行缓解。相关信息可参阅提供的链接。

43934820.article_content:
ADVISORIES
CVE-2025-46336
(
NVD
)
GHSA-9j94-67jr-4cqj
Vendor Advisory
GEM
rack-session
SEVERITY
CVSS v3.x
: 4.2 (
Medium
)
UNAFFECTED VERSIONS
< 2.0.0
PATCHED VERSIONS
>= 2.1.1
DESCRIPTION
Summary
When using the
Rack::Session::Pool
middleware, simultaneous rack
requests can restore a deleted rack session, which allows the
unauthenticated user to occupy that session.
Details
Rack session middleware
prepares the session at the beginning of request, then saves is back
to the store with possible changes applied by host rack application.
This way the session becomes to be a subject of race conditions in
general sense over concurrent rack requests.
Impact
When using the
Rack::Session::Pool
middleware, and provided the
attacker can acquire a session cookie (already a major issue), the
session may be restored if the attacker can trigger a long running
request (within that same session) adjacent to the user logging out,
in order to retain illicit access even after a user has attempted to logout.
Mitigation
Update to the latest version of
rack-session
, or
Ensure your application invalidates sessions atomically by marking
them as logged out e.g., using a
logged_out
flag, instead of
deleting them, and check this flag on every request to prevent reuse, or
Implement a custom session store that tracks session invalidation
timestamps and refuses to accept session data if the session was
invalidated after the request began.
Related
This code was previously part of
rack
in Rack < 3, see
<https://github.com/rack/rack/security/advisories/GHSA-vpfw-47h7-xj4g>
for the equivalent advisory in
rack
(affecting Rack < 3 only).

data.title: Rust Dependencies Scare Me
data.author: chaosprint
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者对Rust语言依赖管理的担忧。尽管Rust的Cargo工具极大地简化了包管理和跨平台开发，但也让开发者容易不经深思熟虑就引入过多依赖。作者提到在项目中使用了诸如Tokio和Axum等流行但复杂的依赖库，结果发现项目依赖的代码总量达到了360万行，而自己写的代码只有1000行左右。这引发了他对如何审核如此庞大代码量的担忧。尽管有人建议将更多功能加入Rust标准库，但这也会带来管理上的负担。作者最终没有找到明确的解决方案，只是提出可能需要对依赖代码进行更多审核，并表达了对Rust相关岗位的兴趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust标准库是否应增加更多功能以及Rust项目中依赖管理的复杂性

不同观点：
• [支持增加标准库功能] demarq认为，许多人呼吁像Go语言一样，在Rust的标准库中添加更多功能，以减少对外部依赖的依赖。这种做法可以简化项目管理，并减少不必要的间接依赖。

• [依赖管理的两难境地] palata指出，虽然Cargo让添加依赖变得非常简单，但这也会导致间接依赖的快速增加，一个依赖可能会引入数十个其他依赖。即使想谨慎管理依赖，也很难避免这种情况。palata提到，在C++中，找到不带有大量间接依赖的依赖库相对容易，可能是因为C++添加依赖更困难，或者其生态系统更成熟。

• [对Rust生态的看法] palata表示，虽然他个人更喜欢Rust语言本身（相比C++），但Rust生态中依赖大量小包的现象似乎不会改变，这是一种遗憾。这意味着开发者必须从互联网上拉取大量代码，以完成项目开发，这是一种权衡。

补充讨论：
• [争议焦点] 争议的核心在于Rust标准库是否应该扩展以减少对外部依赖的依赖，还是保持现有的设计哲学，鼓励使用小而独立的包。这种设计哲学有其优势，但也带来了依赖管理的复杂性。

• [外部链接] stefanos82提到，相关讨论在Hacker News的一个帖子（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43930640）中也有涉及，表明这是一个在社区中被广泛讨论的话题。

总体来看，讨论反映了Rust开发者在语言设计哲学与实际开发体验之间的权衡与思考。

43935067.article_content:
Rust Dependencies Scare Me
I do not pretend to have more experience or understanding than the top level engineers I often see writing blogs here, but what I am is annoyed. I love rust. It's by far my favorite language, I enjoy the community and the language ergonomics. I've been able to incorporate it into projects in my day job where fit.
Rust's dependencies are starting to worry me. For those who don't code in Rust, Rust provides an ecosystem of crates through crates.io, allowing users to helpfully install them with the command cargo add, or by simply adding the requested crate and version to the Cargo.toml file. This paradigm is similar to NPM for nodejs.
The Good
Cargo is helpful and a huge productivity booster, ensuring I don't have to hunt around and link files myself with something like CMake. This also allows me to swap between architectures and operating systems pretty frequently, mainly my M1 macbook air and my x86 Debian desktop. In general I don't have to think much about package management and gets me right into writing code.
The Bad
Not thinking about package management careful makes me sloppy. In a recent production project I pulled in dotenv a crate I've seen many other rust developers use. This worked fine for multiple weeks until recently when checking a rust security advisory mentioning that dotenv is
unmaintained
. Below is a suggested alternative dotenvy. This whole fiasco led me tho think .... do I even need this crate at all? 35 lines later I had the parts of dotenv I needed. Packages become un-mainted in every language and it was my choice to pull in an arguably trivial dependency. So what happens when I have dependencies I do need?
So Much Code
Tokio is one of rust's most well maintained packages of all time. This was added with axum a webserver by the same folks that sits on top of the tokio (the async runtime). Tokio is legitimately one of the coolest things  I've ever gotten to work with, touting itself as a work stealing multithreaded runtime. Tokio has performed leaps and bounds better than I ever could have hoped.
So with that I chose to add a couple more dependencies that I belived were needed, bringing my total cargo file to these
Axum, Reqwest , ripunzip, serde, serde_json, tokio, tower-http, tracing, and tracing-subscriber
In general I considered the project to be trivial, a webserver that handles requests, unzips files, and has logs
In an attempt to build resilient software I decided to vendor my packages, a cargo feature that downloads all my dependencies so I can host them locally.
Out of curiosity I ran
toeki
a tool for counting lines of code, and found a staggering 3.6 million lines of rust. Removing the vendored packages reduces this to 11136 lines of rust.
Now I understand that webservers are complex, and a full asyncronous runtime is even more complex. However the entire linux kernel is 27.8 million lines according to this
register article
That's only 7 of my project....
How could I ever audit all of that code?
The code that I personally wrote is only around 1000 lines
What's the solution?
I have no idea... Many call for adding more to the rust standard library much like Go, however this causes its own set of issues. Rust is positioned as a high performance, safe, and modular language meaning to compete with CPP and C. That means it targets things like embedded devices. Every new thing that gets added to the std library is one more thing for the rust team to have to manage and work on. Just Tokio itself has one of the most active Github and programming discords Ive seen.
I can't rewrite the world, an async runtime and web server are just too difficult and take to long for me to justify writing for a project like this (although I should eventually just for a better understanding).
With a question I've asked during an interview at cloudflare I was told that cloudflare just leverages tokio like everyone else and pulls from crates.io.  How often do they audit that code?
Clickhouse has mentioned problems with
binary sizes
and I doubt they even have the same amount of crates.
With cargo there is no easy way (as far as I can tell) to see what lines ACTUALLY get compiled into the final binary, many crates include items for windows which I don't necessarily need (but there's no official way to tell cargo that).
So now I pose the question to you what do we do?
Hiring for a rust role?  consider me :)

43935486.article_content:
Reporting by Emily Fishbein was supported by the Pulitzer Center.
Heading north in the dark, the only way Gavesh could try to track his progress through the Thai countryside was by watching the road signs zip by. The Jeep’s three occupants—Gavesh, a driver, and a young Chinese woman—had no languages in common, so they drove for hours in nervous silence as they wove their way out of Bangkok and toward Mae Sot, a city on Thailand’s western border with Myanmar.
When they reached the city, the driver pulled off the road toward a small hotel, where another car was waiting. “I had some suspicions—like, why are we changing vehicles?” Gavesh remembers. “But it happened so fast.”
They left the highway and drove on until, in total darkness, they parked at what looked like a private house. “We stopped the vehicle. There were people gathered. Maybe 10 of them. They took the luggage and they asked us to come,” Gavesh says. “One was going in front, there was another one behind, and everyone said: ‘Go, go, go.’”
Gavesh and the Chinese woman were marched through the pitch-black fields by flashlight to a riverside where a boat was moored. By then, it was far too late to back out.
Gavesh’s journey had started, seemingly innocently, with a job ad on Facebook promising work he desperately needed.
Instead, he found himself trafficked into a business commonly known as “pig butchering”—a form of fraud in which scammers form romantic or other close relationships with targets online and extract money from them. The Chinese crime syndicates behind the scams have netted billions of dollars, and they have used violence and coercion to force their workers, many of them people trafficked like Gavesh, to carry out the frauds from large compounds, several of which operate openly in the quasi-lawless borderlands of Myanmar.
We spoke to Gavesh and five other workers from inside the scam industry, as well as anti-trafficking experts and technology specialists. Their testimony reveals how global companies, including American social media and dating apps and international cryptocurrency and messaging platforms, have given the fraud business the means to become industrialized. By the same token, it is Big Tech that may hold the key to breaking up the scam syndicates—if only these companies can be persuaded or compelled to act.
We’re identifying Gavesh using a pseudonym to protect his identity. He is from a country in South Asia, one he asked us not to name. He hasn’t shared his story much, and he still hasn’t told his family. He worries about how they’d handle it.
Until the pandemic, he had held down a job in the tourism industry. But lockdowns had gutted the sector, and two years later he was working as a day laborer to support himself and his father and sister. “I was fed up with my life,” he says. “I was trying so hard to find a way to get out.”

When he saw the Facebook post in mid-2022, it seemed like a godsend. A company in Thailand was looking for English-speaking customer service and data entry specialists. The monthly salary was $1,500—far more than he could earn at home—with meals, travel costs, a visa, and accommodation included. “I knew if I got this job, my life would turn around. I would be able to give my family a good life,” Gavesh says.
What came next was life-changing, but not in the way Gavesh had hoped. The advert was a fraud—and a classic tactic syndicates use to force workers like Gavesh into an economy that operates as something like a dark mirror of the global outsourcing industry.
The true scale of this type of fraud is hard to estimate, but the United Nations
reported
in 2023 that hundreds of thousands of people had been trafficked to work as online scammers in Southeast Asia. One 2024 study, from the University of Texas, estimates that the criminal syndicates that run these businesses have
stolen at least $75 billion
since 2020.
These schemes have been going on for more than two decades, but they’ve started to capture global attention only recently, as the syndicates running them increasingly
shift
from Chinese targets toward the West. looked for ways

data.title: Let's be real about dependencies
data.author: itzlambda
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了编程中依赖管理的问题，特别对比了Rust与传统C/C++的依赖处理方式。作者指出，尽管Rust项目常被抱怨使用大量库（crates），但这种依赖问题在C/C++项目中同样存在，只是由系统而非编译器直接管理。作者通过分析一个C++程序（RViz）的动态库依赖，展示了其复杂的依赖树，包括Qt、Boost、ROS等多个库，表明大型GUI程序在传统语言中同样依赖繁多。文章结论是，依赖管理问题并非Rust独有，只是Rust开发者更直接地面对这些成本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机程序设计中如何处理人类用户的复杂性以及如何在设计中找到平衡

不同观点：
• zahlman认为，文章提出的一个有趣观察是，大型程序往往是那些为人类交互设计的程序，因为人类的复杂性使得让计算机完成人类期望的任务变得困难。他提到有两个观点：一个是人们需要通过学习更简单和更具组合性的原语来更好地理解计算机，从而带来更小、更强大的程序；另一个观点是，如果一个程序被编写一次但被多次使用，程序员投入额外时间降低学习曲线将通过用户节省的时间得到补偿。zahlman认为这两个观点都有道理，设计就是在它们之间找到平衡，且不同的人可能希望有不同的平衡。

• jruohonen则从解决方案的角度出发，提出容器或Ubuntu的snaps可能是例子，虽然没有明确表态这些方案的好坏，但暗示了这些技术可能是应对程序设计复杂性的一种尝试。

补充讨论：
• zahlman强调设计是一个平衡的过程，涉及到程序员与用户之间的权衡，且这种平衡会因人而异。
• jruohonen更关注于实际的技术解决方案，提出了容器技术和snaps作为可能的创新方向，这为原评论中的抽象讨论提供了一个具体的落脚点。
• 争议的焦点可能在于如何在简化用户学习曲线与提高程序性能和功能之间找到最佳平衡，以及哪些技术手段能最有效地实现这一目标。

Introduction
First Attempt

Conclusions
Introduction
I’ve been wanting to do this for a few weeks, ever since I typed
apt install xorg-dev
on my Debian system and it installed
literally 30 megabytes of header files. A perennial complaint among
various sections of the Rust community is “all these darn programs that
use 300 crates to do
anything
”. These complaints are valid, but
my argument is that they’re also not NEW, and they’re certainly not
unique to Rust. Rather the difference in dependencies between something
written in Rust vs. “traditional” C or C++ is that on Unix systems, all
these dependencies are still there, just handled by the system instead
of the compiler directly. The distro maintainers do more of the work,
and our build systems assume the presence of various system libraries in
system places. The only thing new about it is that programmers are
exposed to more of the costs of it up-front.
First Attempt

random Real Life C++ Program What Does Useful Stuff,
RViz

data.title: Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite Benchmarks on Ubuntu Linux vs. AMD vs. Intel
data.author: bomkarram
data.article_summary: 本文总结了Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite在Ubuntu Linux上的性能表现，并与AMD和Intel处理器进行了对比。尽管Snapdragon X Elite最初主要针对Windows 11开发，但Linux社区对其在Linux系统上的表现寄予厚望。在Ubuntu Linux的支持下，Canonical工程师不断改进对X Elite的兼容性，并发布了Ubuntu 25.04的ARM64桌面镜像。作者购买了搭载Snapdragon X Elite的Acer Swift 14 AI笔记本进行测试，结果显示尽管有进展，但整体性能和支持仍不尽如人意。文章详细比较了该处理器在多种应用和基准测试（如浏览器性能、视频编码、AI基准测试等）中的表现，结果显示其在Linux环境下的竞争力不如AMD和Intel的同类产品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Acer Swift 14 AI 及其他搭载 Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite 处理器的笔记本电脑在 Linux 系统上的适用性问题

不同观点：
• **不推荐作为日常使用**：由于 Acer Swift 14 AI 和其他类似笔记本在 Linux 系统上存在许多未实现或缺失的功能（如网络摄像头、音频等），因此不适合作为日常使用设备，除非用户仅进行非常轻量的网页浏览且不关心其他功能。
• **散热和性能问题**：有观点指出，这些设备在长时间负载下会出现过热和自动关机的问题，这对许多用户来说是无法接受的，尤其是在需要稳定性能的日常使用场景中。

补充讨论：
• **目标用户群体有限**：对于仅需要基本网页浏览功能的用户，这些设备可能仍然具有一定的吸引力，但对于有更高要求的用户来说，这些问题使得设备几乎无法使用。
• **功能缺失的具体例子**：特别提到了网络摄像头和音频功能的问题，表明这些缺失的功能对设备的整体实用性有显著影响。
• **Linux 系统的兼容性问题**：讨论中隐含的一点是，这些问题主要存在于 Linux 系统环境下，可能不适用于其他操作系统（如 Windows），因此对于操作系统选择的讨论也可能影响用户的选择。

43934961.article_content:
Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite Benchmarks On Ubuntu Linux vs. AMD vs. Intel
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Processors
on 8 May 2025 at 08:30 AM EDT.
Page 1 of 15
.
30 Comments
.
June 2024 marked the launch of the Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite to much initial fanfare for finally some compelling ARM laptop designs. While initially -- and still to this day with the likes of
the TUXEDO X Elite laptop not materializing yet
-- being focused on Windows 11 on ARM, there was hope among Linux users this would lead to a nice ARM Linux laptop experience, since after all Qualcomm and Linaro were working on enhancing the support for Linux. Now approaching the one year point, the overall state of the Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite support and performance is rather disappointing. Here's a look at where things currently are and performance relative to AMD Ryzen and Intel Core Ultra when making use of the latest Ubuntu Linux support.
Ubuntu Linux has been at the forefront of trying to provide a nice Qualcomm X Elite Linux experience. Going back months they've been
shipping a Ubuntu 24.10 developer preview / concept image
for use on the Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite laptops (Snapdragon X Plus isn't yet supported to the extent of the X Elite SoC) and Canonical engineers worked on
more X1E improvements for Ubuntu 25.04
. They've been relying in large part on the various
Snapdragon X
DeviceTree additions making it into the upstream Linux kernel and other kernel/driver upstream support work for enabling the X Elite SoC support and other components being found in the range of Microsoft Copilot+ AI ARM laptops.
Given the progress being made on the Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite laptop support under Ubuntu Linux and even with
Ubuntu 25.04 now having a nice ARM64 desktop image
, I decided to bite the bullet and buy a Snapdragon X Elite laptop finally for testing at Phoronix, with Qualcomm nor any of the other laptop vendors having stepped up in the nearly year since launch. I ended up buying the Acer Swift 14 AI laptop (SF14-11T-X3RZ). This Snapdragon X Elite X1E-78-100 laptop features the Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite SoC, 16GB of RAM, a 14.5-inch 2560 x 1600 120Hz 300 nits display, and 1TB NVMe SSD.
The Snapdragon X Elite X1E-78-100 SoC features 12 Oryon CPU cores, 42MB total cache, 3.4GHz maximum multi-core frequency without any boost frequency, and a Qualcomm Adreno GPU rated for 3.8 TFLOPS. The Snapdragon X Elite X1E-78-100 is paired with LPDDR5x-8448 MT/s memory.
The Acer Swift 14 AI SF14-11T has for months been supported by the Ubuntu X1E concept images and the other factor in picking this laptop for carrying out my Linux testing was being the most affordable option as of writing: the Acer SF14-11T-X3RZ can be found for $799 USD at some Internet retailers, a discount of $400 off the Acer list price. Used the Acer SF14-11T can be found for around $600+.
After carrying out some Windows 11 on ARM tests for a future article, I then set out to see what the experience was like for the Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite now 11 months after launch. I started off using the Ubuntu 25.04 ARM64 desktop image given its new availability and how well that new ARM64 desktop image was working out on the System76 Thelio Astra. After disabling Secure Boot from the Acer BIOS setup screen, I set out to boot the Ubuntu 25.04 desktop ARM64 ISO off USB. As easy as x86_64!

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在线平台内容审核和言论自由的讨论

不同观点：
• **观点一**：biglyburrito认为平台（如Twitter）应该对内容审核保持中立，特别是对政治言论不应偏袒任何一方。他以Twitter对某些政治人物的言论采取限制措施为例，认为这侵犯了言论自由。他主张平台不应成为“真理仲裁者”，并提到如果平台选择审查某些内容，就应准备面对公众的质疑和批评。

• **观点二**：另一方观点认为，平台有责任对其内容进行审核，以防止虚假信息传播。支持者指出，社交媒体平台上的虚假信息可能会对现实社会产生严重影响，例如煽动暴力或传播有害的阴谋论。因此，平台需要采取措施限制某些有害内容，以维护公共安全和社会稳定。

• **观点三**：还有人提出平台作为私人企业，有权根据其服务条款和社区标准进行内容审核。他们认为，言论自由并不意味着用户可以在任何平台上发表任何言论，平台有权利和责任设定规则，并对违反规则的内容采取行动。

补充讨论：
• **关于偏见的争议**：有讨论指出，内容审核过程中可能存在偏见，尤其是政治偏见。biglyburrito特别提到Twitter可能对某些政治观点（如保守派）采取了不公正的限制措施，而对其他观点（如自由派）则相对宽松。

• **关于透明度和问责制的讨论**：一些评论者提到，平台在进行内容审核时应保持更高的透明度，并建立明确的问责机制，以便用户能够理解和挑战平台的决定。

• **关于法律和监管的讨论**：有观点认为，政府应介入并制定相关法律，以规范社交媒体平台的内容审核行为，确保其公正性和合法性。然而，也有人担心这可能会导致过度监管，从而影响言论自由。

• **关于技术解决方案的讨论**：一些评论者建议，平台可以采用更先进的技术手段，如人工智能和机器学习，来更有效地识别和处理有害内容，同时减少人工审核可能带来的偏见问题。

争议焦点：平台内容审核的合理范围以及如何在言论自由和防止虚假信息之间取得平衡。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在只能选择一个手机应用程序的情况下，哪一个应用最为重要或实用。

不同观点：
• Kuyawa认为选择一个功能全面的应用（如Brave浏览器）是最佳选择，因为它集成了AI、地图、银行、加密钱包、聊天等多种功能，几乎可以满足所有需求，即使不能满足，也可以通过其构建新功能。
• Walthamstow则更看重免费的电话和短信功能，并认为可以通过电脑进行银行业务，而且自己所在地区公共交通便利，不太依赖Uber等打车应用。
• Anenefan来自农村地区，认为最重要的是一个无需移动网络即可获取位置、时间和速度的GPS程序，这对于在偏远地区活动至关重要。
• Quinzel选择Safari浏览器，认为通过浏览器可以访问大多数其他服务，即使导航功能差一些，但至少能保持连接。
• Davydm强调银行业务的便捷性，不愿意回到实体银行浪费时间，虽然会错过各种消息渠道，但可以告知他人只能通过短信联系。
• AznHisoka最看重多因素认证（MFA）应用，这表明其对安全性的高度关注。
• Almosthere假设手机只是一个功能而非应用，那么地图应用是最重要的。
• Shakna和Cranberryturkey都简单表明最看重消息应用和Safari浏览器。

补充讨论：
• 地理位置对应用选择的影响：Anenefan强调其农村地区背景，使得GPS程序成为首选。
• 对银行业务的不同看法：Kuyawa认为可以通过AI构建相关功能，而Davydm则明确表示不愿回到实体银行。
• 争议的焦点：不同用户对应用的需求和优先级有显著差异，主要取决于各自的生活环境（城市与农村）和个人偏好（功能全面性、安全性、连接性等）。

data.title: Mycoria is an open and secure overlay network that connects all participants
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: Mycoria是一个开放、安全的覆盖网络，旨在重现早期互联网的自由探索精神。其核心价值包括平等连接、无官僚主义限制、全员欢迎、所有通信经过认证和加密，确保无监控和无障碍连接。用户可以通过互联网接入或扩展为自己的网状网络。其设计目标是保持小巧简单，兼容现有基础设施，默认安全和隐私保护（部分功能仍在开发中）。主要功能包括自动端到端加密、现代加密技术、智能可扩展路由、.myco域名解析、简单服务发现和网络自动优化/修复。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mycoria项目的技术细节、隐私性、扩展性及其与其他类似项目的比较

不同观点：
• 作者@dhaavi认为Mycoria是一个可扩展的layer-3 mesh网络，具备隐私和安全性，是在吸收了cjdns和Yggdrasil的经验后开发的。项目目前处于MVP阶段，但未来会有更多发展。
• @namecast担心Mycoria中基于地理位置的前缀可能被用于实施政策限制，建议使用基于延迟的前缀以避免地理标记带来的潜在问题。
• @mattlondon对去中心化网络持保留态度，担心被用于非法活动如分享儿童色情内容，并对是否会无意中协助路由此类内容表示担忧。
• @ramaro关心Mycoria是否需要使用防火墙来限制端口访问，类似于Yggdrasil的要求。
• @pidgeon_lover将Mycoria与zrok进行比较，关注其默认隐私设置。
• @theknarf提到Veilid，询问Mycoria与之相比的异同。
• @areyourllysorry建议作者将精力投入已有网络如i2p，而不是创建新的网络。
• @csande17质疑Mycoria是否试图隐藏公共互联网IP地址，并对其路由方案表示不解。
• @thenthenthen关注Mycoria如何应对DNS中毒等问题，如GFW的做法。
• @9dev提到Reticulum项目，询问Mycoria与其网络层的重叠程度。
• @elia_42对作者处理可扩展路由的方法表示赞赏。
• @OsrsNeedsf2P关注Mycoria的平均延迟，并将其与I2P和Tor进行比较。
• @tornadofart总结Mycoria是一种叠加隐私和网络中立性的互联网，并询问其主要用例及与Yggdrasil和VPN的区别。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是地理位置前缀可能带来的政策限制问题，以及是否应采用基于延迟的前缀来避免这些限制。
• 另一个争议点在于去中心化网络的潜在非法使用问题，以及如何防止和应对这种情况。
• 不同用户对Mycoria的隐私性、默认设置及其与其他类似项目（如Yggdrasil、zrok、Veilid、i2p）的区别表示关注。
• 技术细节如路由方案、延迟、IP地址隐藏等也是讨论的重点，用户对项目的具体实现和应用场景有较多疑问。

通过这些讨论，可以看出Mycoria作为一个新项目，在技术实现、隐私性、扩展性及应用场景方面引发了广泛关注和不同角度的思考。

Mycoria is an open and secure overlay network that connects all participants. It values freedom of connectivity and aims to imitate the curious and adventurous spirit of the early Internet:
Everyone is equal
: Easily connect to anyone
Everyone is welcome
: Open network without bureaucracy
No spooking: Everthing is authenticated
No surveillance: Everything is encrypted (+ Private Addresses!)
No barriers: Connect via the Internet or extend Mycoria with your own mesh
Design Goals
Keep it small and simple
Compatible with existing infrastructure (eg. DNS)
Secure by default
Private by default (WIP)
Features
Automatic end-to-end encryption
Modern cryptography
Smart and scalable routing
Dashboard
Resolve .myco DNS (OS configuration required)
Simple Service Discovery
Auto-Optimization/Healing of Network (for Internet overlay) (WIP)
Rotating private addresses (WIP)
Continue reading about the concept.
Dashboard Impressions

data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
2025年5月5日，作者推出了“Mac Themes Garden”网站，展示超过3000个经典Mac时代的Kaleidoscope主题，供浏览、下载和探索。网站还提供RSS订阅源，方便用户跟踪主题的更新。该项目源于作者几年前运行的Mac Themes Bot，最初在Bluesky、Mastodon和Cohost上展示Mac OS X和经典Mac主题。由于Twitter上的相关账号被封，作者开始从Wayback Machine抓取Kaleidoscope主题数据。

作者手动截图并记录约4000个主题的信息，包括作者和发布年份，使用UTM.app运行Mac OS 9虚拟机进行操作。由于自动化困难，大部分工作需手动完成。尽管尚未完成所有主题的录入，但在朋友的鼓励下，作者于今年1月开始制作网站，现已上线。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于早期Mac和Windows系统主题定制文化的回顾与比较，以及对现代操作系统缺乏类似定制功能的感慨。

不同观点：
• **rhet0rica**：对Mac主题创作社区的多样性和创作者的 industriousness 感到震惊，尤其是与同期Windows社区的对比。他认为Windows社区的定制文化相对单一，且主要集中在少数技术爱好者中，而Mac社区则展现了更广泛的创造力和多样性。他特别提到Martha Royer的创作，并表达了对NeXT主题的渴望。

• **cosmic_cheese**：怀念Classic Mac OS的Kaleidoscope方案和外观管理器主题，认为这些定制功能带来的灵活性在现代操作系统中难以复现。尽管承认Classic Mac OS的安全问题，但他认为可以通过类似现代macOS的扩展架构来实现更安全的定制功能。

• **red_admiral**：对所有平台上曾经存在的自定义颜色和主题功能表示怀念，指出即使是桌面Linux在定制性上也难以与过去的Classic Mac OS相比。他批评GNOME的单一主题策略，认为这剥夺了用户个性化选择的机会。

• **rf15**：回忆儿时定制Mac和Windows机器的主题，感叹如今只剩下“企业赞助的平淡无奇”和不关心个性化定制的用户群体。

• **Lammy**：非常怀念可以随意修改Finder和系统键盘快捷键的时代，提到使用ResEdit进行系统定制。

• **hoistbypetard**：表示愿意付费以在Linux上使用经典Mac OS 8/9主题，显示出对过去主题的强烈怀旧情感。

• **bix6**：怀念Monkey Paradise主题，表达对过去主题的怀旧。

• **milesskorpen**：回忆过去与Winamp主题一起使用的日子，不确定是自己变老了还是技术发展导致这种定制文化的消失。

• **doodpants**：怀念Kaleidoscope并自豪地分享自己创作的主题Crayon OS。

• **WillAdams**：怀念Mac OS 9中窗口标题栏在“window-shaded”时缩小到文字大小的功能，认为这是他最怀念的Mac OS 9特性。

• **antfarm**：回忆使用Kaleidoscope将PowerMac风格化为BeOS，并提到使用扩展实现Finder中的column浏览器功能。
