• 怀旧情感：多数评论者对过去的主题定制文化表示怀念，并对现代操作系统缺乏类似功能感到遗憾。
• 技术实现：部分评论者讨论了在现代系统中实现类似定制功能的技术可行性，提出了通过扩展架构实现更安全定制的可能性。

43919868.article_content:
Introducing Mac Themes Garden!
May 5th, 2025
The short version
I've "launched" the
Mac Themes Garden
! It is a website showcasing more than 3,000 (and counting) Kaleidoscope from the Classic Mac era, ready to be seen, downloaded and explored! Check it out! Oh, and there also is an
RSS feed
you can subscribe to see themes as they are added/updated!
And yes, there is a button that you can include on your website!
Grab it here
! Isn't it cute?
Now, for the yapping.
Note: if you're reading this in an RSS reader, you might want to open the article on my website directly as it contains a bunch of CSS demos and those won't work well in an RSS reader.
Some background
If you know me from Online, you may know that I've been running the Mac Themes Bot on
Bluesky
/
Mastodon
/
Cohost
for a few years now.
The idea of the bot was simple, showcasing custom themes from the Mac OS X and Classic Mac eras, on the rate of one an hour. Since I was inspired by
@kaleidoscopemac
on Twitter, I only started showcasing themes made for
ShapeShifter by Unsanity
. A while later, that Twitter account got suspended.
Since I already had the
tooling in place
to scrape and post themes for OS X, I figured I could add themes for Kaleidoscope (OS 7/8/9) into the mix. After trying (and failing) to get the original dataset from the author of the bot, I set on to scrape the Wayback Machine for records of the
Kaleidoscope Scheme Archive
.
From that point on, my bot would post themes every hour, with a classic theme on even hours and an OS X theme on odd hours
[1]
.
The years passed, the bot carried on, made me and a bunch of other people smile on the various websites where I would run it. The
Cohost
incarnation in particular was really special because Cohost was a special site, but also it was full of nerds (complimentary) and people would go nuts for the random gems in there.
Around maybe early 2023, I grew frustrated of the fact that the only images I had for the Kaleidoscope
themes
schemes were those
tiny .gif files
from the late 90s.
"Recording" 25-year-old schemes
So I did the reasonable thing: set up a terribly manual process to take screenshots and record the author information of the
~4,000 themes available
, with the intention of making a website showcasing everything once I was done.
Without going into details (which you can read
here
), the process looks like this:
Open my Mac OS 9 VM in
UTM.app
(QEMU frontend)
Go through the folder of schemes
Select a given scheme, apply it
Take 3 screenshots:
One of the scheme's about box.
One of the scheme being used in the Finder/regular desktop situation.
And finally, a screenshot of the application
KSA Sampler
in order to mimic the original screenshots from the Kaleidoscope Scheme Archive. That specific screenshot would get pasted into Photoshop to be cropped/trimmed of its opaque background using Photoshop Actions.
Write down the name, author and release year of the scheme
Find the corresponding .sit archive file
Record all of this in a record inside an Airtable database.
Here's how it looks inside Airtable:
6 rows inside an Airtable database, showing screenshots and scheme informations
On a good day, I can maybe record, I don't know, a dozen or so themes an hour.
But Damien, why didn't you automate this process?!
I'm glad you asked! I tried! But I, at least until now, could not find a good way to reliably perform the actions I need to take. And that's not even touching on the fact that sometimes a scheme doesn't have any author or year information! Sometimes the author inside the Kaleidoscope scheme file is completely wrong, and the actual author is written in a separate "Read me" file. Sometimes there's barely any information to go by, sometimes the scheme is buggy and would crash my VM.
At that point, the only automations I have are:
a
Keyboard Maestro
macro
that calls the
qemu-monitor
for the running VM, takes a lossless screenshot and puts it into my clipboard, ready to be pasted
Photoshop actions to:
create a document from the clipboard
after cropping, remove all pixels of a given color in a document and trim it to remove extra alpha pixels (for the KSA Sampler screenshots above)
A
Quickeys
shortcut to call "Hide Others" inside of Mac OS 9. Turns out this action didn't have a keyboard shortcut until Mac OS X? Didn't know that!
Beyond that, I'm afraid it's all manual since I want to record data that isn't straight forwardly extracted by just looking at files 😔.
At any rate
, I was and thought "I'll finish recording all these schemes,
and then
I'll make the website"...
Dear reader, I am not done. By my own estimations, I am maybe halfway done. I do not know when I will be fully done, but my good friend
Sage
pushed me to: make the damn website already.
And they were right, I should have made the website earlier! It was a fun and challenging distraction, and
fuck me
I could use distractions these days.
Making Da Website
So, around January of this year, I've started work on the website.

data.title: I can’t understand Apple’s Critical Alert policy (2023)
data.author: logistra
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了一位开发者推出了名为SuperDose的iOS应用，用于提醒用户按时服药。由于应用需要在不干扰"勿扰模式"的情况下发送重要提醒，开发者申请访问苹果的Critical Alerts API，但遭到拒绝。苹果给出的理由是该应用无法确保用户正确使用API，而开发者认为这不合理，因为Critical Alerts需要用户明确同意才能启用，且苹果自己的Health应用也使用这一功能。此外，开发者发现一些其他类型的提醒应用却获得了批准，令他感到困惑和沮丧。他担心没有这一权限，用户可能因手机静音而错过关键药物提醒，带来潜在危险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的Critical Alerts API权限分配及开发者对其的争议

不同观点：
• **Zealotux的观点**：用户应该能够为特定应用（如药物提醒应用）授予权限以覆盖静音模式，类似于紧急联系人权限。
• **os2warpman的观点**：只有最重要的通知（如紧急医疗情况、火灾报警）才应使用Critical Alerts，像药物提醒这种优先级不够高，不应该获得该权限。
• **bArray的观点**：Apple可能因为竞争原因拒绝提供API权限，尤其当该应用与其自有产品（如Health应用）存在竞争时。
• **uni_baconcat的观点**：除了Apple的第一方应用，只有极少数第三方应用（如地震警报应用）获得了Critical Alerts权限。
• **nottorp的观点**：Apple会因功能重叠而持续拒绝某些应用的API请求。
• **zug_zug的观点**：Apple需要改进其审核和申诉流程，并制定明确的官方标准，以维护其生态系统的健康。
• **petercooper的观点**：Apple的很多决定对用户来说是不透明的，虽然可能有其商业或法规上的原因，但缺乏解释让用户难以理解。
• **SuperShibe的观点**：在欧盟，可以利用DMA（数字市场法）来解决此类API访问问题。
• **nazgu1的观点**：Apple在CarPlay等功能上也存在类似的限制，用户应该有权选择是否接收关键提醒通知，而不是由Apple全权控制。
• **bitpush的观点**：Apple偏袒自家应用，允许它们使用私有API，而第三方开发者往往受制于Apple的审核流程，难以获得公平待遇。
• **mimsee的观点**：如果HomeAssistant的iOS应用可以访问Critical Alerts API，那么药物提醒应用也应该可以。
• **dinkblam的观点**：App Store的审核过程存在随机性和偏袒，有些无关紧要的应用也能获得Critical Alerts权限。
• **xtajv的观点**：Critical Alerts API旨在替代或补充公共紧急警报系统，限制其使用是必要的，以防止滥用和确保公共安全通知的及时性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Apple对Critical Alerts API的严格控制，开发者认为这种控制缺乏透明度和公平性，尤其是当Apple自家应用能够使用类似功能时。
• 一些用户和开发者呼吁Apple改进其审核流程，增加透明度，并提供更明确的指导方针。
• 欧盟的数字市场法（DMA）被提及为可能的解决方案，显示出法规在技术平台治理中的潜在作用。

43922698.article_content:
I can't understand Apple's Critical Alert policy
08 May, 2025
Last week, I launched an iOS app called
SuperDose
— a simple medication reminder that sends notifications to users when it's time to take their meds.
For the app to function properly, it needs access to the Critical Alerts API. Critical Alerts allow notifications to bypass silent mode and Do Not Disturb, which is essential for users who take life-saving medications like those for hypertension.
Apple’s own Health app uses Critical Alerts for its medication reminders, so I assumed my use case would qualify. I submitted a request for access to the API, but it was rejected.
The rejection email said, "Apps that can't enforce that usage are not likely candidates for this API." That reasoning makes no sense to me — Critical Alerts can only be enabled with explicit user consent. If Apple’s concern is abuse, the opt-in mechanism already covers that. By this logic, even the Health app shouldn't be allowed to use it.
What’s even more confusing is that I’ve seen general-purpose to-do or reminder apps on the App Store that somehow got approved for Critical Alerts, even though their use case seems far less urgent.
Without this permission, my app is incomplete. Users might miss critical medication reminders just because their phone was on silent. That’s potentially dangerous.
Honestly, I’m a bit frustrated.

data.title: Extending a Language – Writing Powerful Macros in Scheme
data.author: textread
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Scheme中编写强大的宏，特别强调了Scheme宏机制的独特优势——内置的**卫生**特性，使得宏能够无缝融入语言本身。文章首先介绍了前提知识，包括Chez Scheme、Emacs、Org、Geiser、Paredit等工具的配置和使用。接着，文章通过简单的宏示例逐步引导读者，如变量自增、追踪let绑定、访问向量位置等。然后，文章深入探讨了**语法对象**和**syntax-case宏**，包括如何打破卫生机制及不同阶段的标识符引用。最后，文章介绍了扩展功能，如别名、语法参数、标识符属性，并提供了复杂示例，如用Scheme宏实现LR(1)解析器生成器。本文旨在帮助读者掌握Scheme宏的编写，并鼓励语言设计者引入类似机制以增强语言的表达力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Scheme语法中`trace-let`的格式修改建议及对编程语言中全大写命名惯例的讨论。

不同观点：
• 第一个观点由neilv提出，建议对`trace-let`的语法做一些格式修改，例如将语法规则模板中的模式变量全部改为大写，并增加一些缩进。他还建议将命名`let`变量命名为"loop"或以"loop-"为前缀，以提高可读性和一致性。他提供了具体的代码示例来展示这些修改，如使用`loop`进行递归调用，以及调整显示和缩进的顺序。
   
• 第二个观点是neilv对全大写命名惯例的批评，尤其是对Java中常量使用全大写命名的做法。他认为这种做法源于C预处理器宏的传统，但在Java中使用这种惯例是一种错误，因为Java和C是两种不同的语言，且Java的实际使用者与C/C++开发者的背景和需求不同。他呼吁其他语言和API开发者停止使用全大写命名常量和枚举值。

补充讨论：
• neilv认为全大写在Scheme模式变量中的使用是合理的，甚至是最佳实践之一，因为这样能区分不同类型的变量，并提高代码的可读性。
• 对于Java使用全大写命名常量，neilv认为这是一种不必要的模仿，且对代码可读性没有实质性的帮助。他还提到这种惯例在Java中已经根深蒂固，难以改变。

争议焦点：
• 全大写命名常量在不同编程语言中的适用性。neilv明确反对在Java中使用全大写命名常量，认为这是对C/C++惯例的错误继承，并对现代Java开发者没有实际帮助。

总结：
neilv在评论中主要提出了对`trace-let`语法格式修改的建议，并深入讨论了全大写命名惯例在不同编程语言中的合理性，特别是对Java常量命名惯例的批评。他认为在Scheme中使用全大写模式变量是合理的，但在Java中使用全大写常量命名则是过时的做法。

The canonical HTML-formatted version of this document can be found at

1.
Preface
This document is an introduction to writing powerful macros in Scheme.
It was initially written on the occasion of a tutorial I give at the
BOB2023 Konferenz
in Berlin on 17 March 2023.
The macro facility, especially its built-in
hygiene
, is one of the
fundamental pillars of the Scheme programming language.  While more
complicated than the simple token-replacing macros of other languages
like C, Scheme macros can be written in a way that make them robust
and so that the abstractions they offer seamless blend into the
language and cannot be distinguished from syntactic forms built into
the language.  It is often felt that this expressiveness makes writing
Scheme macros more complicated (even something of a black art) than
writing C or Common Lisp macros, for example.  One goal of this
tutorial is to convince the audience otherwise.
While the Scheme macro facility has always been avant-garde (and this
is one of the reasons why Scheme was chosen as the implementation
language for this tutorial), a lot of what is said here also applies
to languages that provide corresponding features.  It is also a appeal
to language designers that languages should include a macro facility
as Scheme does, as this allows for small language cores and enables
the user to provide their own syntactic abstractions.
Another reason why the Scheme language is used in this tutorial is
that it has an exceptionally clear semantics, is a compact language,
and is easy to learn.
The document can both be read as is or used interactively in an Emacs
session.  In the following section, a possible setup is described.
2.
Prerequisites
2.1.
Chez Scheme
We need a Scheme implementation.  This tutorial assumes
Chez Scheme
,
which is one of the most mature, standard-compliant Scheme
implementations.  You can get Chez Scheme from its homepage.  On
Debian-based GNU/Linux system like Ubuntu, it is prepackaged.
2.2.
Emacs
We will use
GNU Emacs
as our development environment, which has great
tooling for Scheme.  The typical GNU/Linux system ships with it.
For GNU Emacs < 28, enable the
NonGNU Emacs Lisp Package Archive
in
your
init file
or
customize
the variable
package-archives
.
Likewise, enable the
NonGNU-devel ELPA Packages
.
2.3.
Org
Org Mode
is a GNU Emacs major mode that allows to document, edit and
execute source code.
The current versions of Org packaged with Emacs hide Scheme evaluation
errors.  This is fixed in the version in Org's git repository, for
which Org
provides installation instructions
.
Familiarize yourself with how one works with
source code in an Org
document
, especially how to
edit
and
execute code
.
2.4.
Geiser
Geiser
is a GNU Emacs package that allows to runs Scheme processes in
GNU Emacs, and which is used by Org's Babel.  To install it, it is
enough to install the package
geiser-chez
using GNU Emacs'
package
menu
.  We need the most recent development version.
2.5.
Paredit
Paredit
, a tool for parenthetical editing in Emacs makes working with
Scheme code a lot more pleasant.  Like Geiser, it can be installed
through GNU Emacs' package manager.
2.6.
Initialization

them for our needs.  The following should go into your init file
unless you want to execute the following code every time you start GNU

data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Ozempic等减肥药物及其相关公司（如Weight Watchers）的讨论，涉及药物的长期效果、公司经营策略、药物依赖性以及健康生活方式的争议。

不同观点：
• **公司债务问题**：cmcaleer认为Weight Watchers的问题源于13年前举债15亿美元回购股票，导致公司长期背负债务，最终濒临破产，而非仅仅是Ozempic的问题。djd20对此表示赞同，并指出公司失去客户是因为用户体验差和不断变化的计划。

• **药物效果及依赖性**：pmarreck分享个人经历，表示在停用Mounjaro药物后体重反弹，重新使用后效果不佳，警告这些药物可能只有一次性效果。snapcaster对Ozempic持矛盾态度，一方面为朋友通过药物成功减肥感到高兴，另一方面担心药物依赖性及生活方式的改变。lanfeust6补充，药物并非万能，体重可能在手术或药物停用后反弹，强调饮食习惯改变的重要性。

• **健康生活方式争议**：tlogan认为GLP-1药物在减少酒精消费方面有显著效果。ChildOfChaos和damnesian则表示，通过控制饮食等自然方式减肥更经济且可持续，面对昂贵的药物，他们更愿意选择调整饮食习惯。

• **药物长期影响及市场问题**：codr7批评Weight Watchers等公司通过制造“回头客”来盈利，可能导致更多饮食失调问题。glp1guide提到Eli Lilly正在起诉药物合成商，试图关闭法律漏洞，并指出药物专利到期时间。

补充讨论：
• **药物与激素作用**：toomuchtodo指出，过去围绕饮食和运动的减肥努力可能忽略了激素和大脑化学作用，GLP-1药物揭示了新的减肥机制。

• **公司重组与未来策略**：mrcwinn希望公司能在重组过程中找到可持续的瘦身方法。

data.article_summary: **sectorlisp** 是一个精简到 512 字节的 LISP 实现，能够在裸机上启动约翰·麦卡锡的元循环求值器。该项目旨在通过三个方面简化 LISP：提供一个纯表达式的 LISP 实现，仅使用语言的核心功能；提供可读的 C 语言参考实现，展示如何在 POSIX 平台上启动元循环求值器；以及一个可以在个人电脑 BIOS 上启动的 512 字节 i8086 汇编 LISP 实现。用户可以通过 `make` 命令生成可启动的 `sectorlisp.bin` 文件，并使用模拟器如 Das Blinkenlights 或 QEMU 运行。该项目提供了详细的代码示例和演示视频。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在引导扇区中实现Lisp语言的可能性和意义

不同观点：
• **gitroom** 认为在引导扇区这样有限的空间内实现Lisp听起来很不可思议。他对在这种受限环境下能实现多少功能表示怀疑，并提出质疑：这种限制到底是推动了更好的解决方案，还是仅仅不必要地增加了难度。

• **隐含的观点**：有些人可能认为这种技术挑战是有价值的，因为它可能会推动创新，迫使开发者在资源有限的情况下找到高效的解决方案。这种限制可能激发出独特的编程技巧和优化方法。

补充讨论：
• **dang** 提供了相关的讨论链接，指向一个之前关于Sectorlisp的讨论帖（2023年1月，8条评论），表明这一话题在技术社区中已经引起了一些关注和讨论。

• **cassepipe** 提供了与该话题相关的博客文章链接，为讨论提供了进一步的技术背景和细节，帮助其他参与者更深入地理解Sectorlisp的具体实现和应用场景。

争议的焦点：主要集中在资源限制是否能够推动技术进步，还是在实际开发中仅仅带来了不必要的困难。这涉及到对技术挑战的价值判断以及在极端约束下进行开发的实际可行性和意义。

sectorlisp
sectorlisp is a 512-byte implementation of LISP that's able to bootstrap
John McCarthy's meta-circular evaluator on bare metal.
Overview
LISP has been described as the
Maxwell's equations of
software
.
Yet there's been very little focus to date on reducing these equations
to their simplest possible form. Even the
original LISP
paper
from the 1960's defines LISP with nonessential elements, e.g.
LABEL
.
This project aims to solve that by doing three things:
We provide a LISP implementation that's written in LISP, as a single
pure expression, using only the essential functions of the language.
See
lisp.lisp
. It's the same meta-circular evaluator in
John McCarthy's paper from the 1960's, except with its bugs fixed,
dependencies included, and syntactic sugar removed.
We provide a readable portable C reference implementation to show how
the meta-circular evaluator can be natively bootstrapped on POSIX
conforming platforms, with a pleasant readline-like interface. See
lisp.c
.
We provide a 512-byte i8086 implementation of LISP that boots from
BIOS on personal computers. See
sectorlisp.S
. To the
best of our knowledge, this is the tiniest true LISP implementation
to date.
Getting Started
See
lisp.lisp
for code examples that you can copy and paste
into your LISP REPL.
You can run the C implementation as follows:
$ make
$ ./lisp
After running
make
you should see a
sectorlisp.bin
file, which is a
master boot record you can put on a flopy disk and boot from BIOS. If
you would prefer to run it in an emulator, we recommend using
Das Blinkenlights
.
curl --compressed https://justine.lol/blinkenlights/blinkenlights-latest.com
>
blinkenlights.com
chmod +x blinkenlights.com
./blinkenlights.com -rt sectorlisp.bin
Alternatively you may use QEMU as follows:
qemu-system-i386 -nographic -fda sectorlisp.bin
Further information may be found on
our wiki
.
Demo
The video above demonstrates how to boot sectorlisp in the blinkenlights
emulator, to bootstrap the meta-circular evaluator, which evaluates a
program for finding the first element in a tree.
You can
watch the full demo on YouTube
.

data.title: Sofie: open-source web based system for automating live TV news production
data.author: rjmunro
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一个Sofie系统的用户指南，介绍了其功能、安装及操作方法。此外，还提供了针对开发者的文档，说明如何为Sofie代码库做贡献。文章还列出了Sofie系统的当前、过去及未来版本信息。最后，邀请用户加入Slack社区，与其他开发者和用户交流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源电视新闻广播自动化系统Sofie的特性、优缺点及其与其他商业系统的比较

不同观点：
• [chriscjcj] 从电视新闻导播的专业角度出发，希望看到Sofie与主要竞争产品（如Ross OverDrive、Sony ELC和Grass Valley Ignite）的特性对比。他认为由于这些系统的复杂性，电视台通常不愿意更换系统，但“免费”可能是一个驱动因素。同时指出支持硬件的限制可能是采用该开源软件的痛点，因为用户可能被迫选择他们不喜欢的硬件。

• [hiatus] 关注Sofie在动态回放处理方面的能力，尤其是在直播过程中，主持人可能临时决定重播某段采访或播放带有解说的片段。他质疑操作员如何在Sofie中处理这种实时更新和覆盖操作，通常这种功能由EVS系统处理。

• [stephen_g] 赞赏Sofie的开源性质和选择CasparCG作为后端播出服务器的做法，认为这是对昂贵商业系统的良好替代。他还提到SuperConductor作为一个类似的相关自动化系统，分享了一些代码和库。

• [eddyg] 提到Sofie的提词器可以通过Joycon控制，展示了该系统在用户界面和操作灵活性方面的独特功能。

• [arboles] 对Sofie是否支持实时编写实时着色器提出疑问，这涉及系统在图形处理和高级视觉效果方面的能力。

• [revskill] 表示对Sofie中Ruby代码的可读性感到满意，暗示了对该系统代码质量和可维护性的认可。

• [fitsumbelay] 认为Sofie使用MeteorJS是一个有趣的技术选择，可能是在讨论该框架对系统开发和性能的影响。

• [tdhz77] 表示计划使用Sofie创建一个AI电视站，显示出对该系统在自动化和人工智能应用方面的潜力感兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Sofie支持的硬件有限，可能导致用户需要选择他们不熟悉的设备，这是开源软件在广播行业应用中的一个挑战。
• 另一个讨论点是Sofie在处理动态直播内容（如实时回放和剪辑播放）方面的能力，用户关心其是否能与商业系统如EVS媲美。
• 系统使用的技术栈（如Ruby代码、MeteorJS框架）和代码质量也得到了不同程度的关注和认可。
• 最后，Sofie在人工智能电视站方面的潜在应用展示了其在未来技术发展中的可能性。

data.title: ALICE detects the conversion of lead into gold at the LHC
data.author: miiiiiike
data.article_summary: ALICE合作组在LHC中通过近距错过的高能铅核碰撞，观测到铅转化为金的核嬗变现象。这一过程通过电磁场诱导的光子-核相互作用实现，铅核中的质子被高能光子激发并弹出，从而将铅（82个质子）转化为金（79个质子）。尽管产生的金核仅存在极短暂时间，研究显示LHC每秒可产生约89,000个金核。在LHC的第二次运行期间（2015-2018年），共产生了约860亿个金核，但总质量仅为29皮克，远不足以用于实际应用。该研究验证了电磁解离的理论模型，并有助于理解和优化LHC的性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：粒子加速器中金元素的产生及其意义，技术进步的局限性，以及炼金术的历史和文化关联。

不同观点：
• **粒子加速器产生金元素的实际意义**：
  - [omnee] 提到在LHC中产生了微量的金元素，虽然量极少，但象征着炼金术梦想的实现。
  - [elashri] 通过计算表明，即使在理想条件下，LHC需要1850亿年才能产生足够支付未来环形对撞机（FCC）的金元素，暗示实际应用不现实。

• **技术进步的局限性**：
  - [cookingmyserver] 认为当前技术进步更多受限于资源和工程能力，而非知识。并指出在生物化学和生物学领域仍有大量未知，这些领域可能带来更多实用知识。
  - [dclowd9901] 对比了粒子加速器炼金与数字货币挖矿，认为后者更具经济效益，暗示当前技术应用的偏差。

• **炼金术的历史和文化关联**：
  - [John23832] 提出历史上的炼金师为何专注于将铅转变为金，而不是其他元素，质疑这可能与两者都是重金属有关。
  - [DrScientist] 开玩笑地暗示LHC的真实目的是实现物理学家炼金的梦想，提到牛顿也曾沉迷于炼金术。

• **未来科技对社会的影响**：
  - [tarkin2] 和 [comrade1234] 都提到了如果金元素的大量人工生产成为现实，可能对全球财富和经济体系产生巨大影响，类似于科幻小说的情节。
  - [725686] 感叹历史上炼金师的思想超前，虽然方法不同，但目标一致。

补充讨论：
• **核反应与其他元素转化**：
  - [billiam] 提到法国的核反应堆不仅用于发电，还通过核反应将铀转化为钚，暗示核反应在元素转化中的广泛应用。

争议焦点：
• **技术应用的实际性和优先级**：部分评论质疑通过粒子加速器产生金元素的实际意义和经济可行性，认为当前技术更应关注其他领域的突破。

News
News
Topic:
Physics
Voir en
français
ALICE detects the conversion of lead into gold at the LHC
Near-miss collisions between high-energy lead nuclei at the LHC generate intense electromagnetic fields that can knock out protons and transform lead into fleeting quantities of gold nuclei
8 May, 2025
Picture of the ALICE detector (image: CERN)
In a paper published in
Physical Review Journals
, the
ALICE collaboration
reports measurements that quantify the transmutation of lead into gold in CERN’s
Large Hadron Collider
(LHC).
Transforming the base metal lead into the precious metal gold was a dream of medieval alchemists. This long-standing quest, known as
chrysopoeia
, may have been motivated by the observation that dull grey, relatively abundant lead is of a similar density to gold, which has long been coveted for its beautiful colour and rarity. It was only much later that it became clear that lead and gold are distinct chemical elements and that chemical methods are powerless to transmute one into the other.
With the dawn of nuclear physics in the 20th century, it was discovered that heavy elements could transform into others, either naturally, by radioactive decay, or in the laboratory, under a bombardment of neutrons or protons. Though gold has been artificially produced in this way before, the ALICE collaboration has now measured the transmutation of lead into gold by a new mechanism involving near-miss collisions between lead nuclei at the LHC.
Extremely high-energy collisions between lead nuclei at the LHC can create quark–gluon plasma, a hot and dense state of matter that is thought to have filled the universe around a millionth of a second after the Big Bang, giving rise to the matter we now know. However, in the far more frequent interactions where the nuclei just miss each other without “touching”, the intense electromagnetic fields surrounding them can induce photon–photon and photon–nucleus interactions that open
further
avenues of exploration.
The electromagnetic field emanating from a lead nucleus is particularly strong because the nucleus contains 82 protons, each carrying one elementary charge. Moreover, the very high speed at which lead nuclei travel in the LHC (corresponding to 99.999993% of the speed of light) causes the electromagnetic field lines to be squashed into a thin pancake, transverse to the direction of motion, producing a short-lived pulse of photons. Often, this triggers a process called electromagnetic dissociation, whereby a photon interacting with a nucleus can excite oscillations of its internal structure, resulting in the ejection of small numbers of neutrons and protons. To create gold (a nucleus containing 79 protons), three protons must be removed from a lead nucleus in the LHC beams.
“It is impressive to see that our detectors can handle head-on collisions producing thousands of particles, while also being sensitive to collisions where only a few particles are produced at a time, enabling the study of electromagnetic ‘nuclear transmutation’ processes,” says Marco Van Leeuwen, ALICE spokesperson.
The ALICE team used the detector’s zero degree calorimeters (ZDC) to count the number of photon–nucleus interactions that resulted in the emission of zero, one, two and three protons accompanied by at least one neutron, which are associated with the production of lead, thallium, mercury and gold, respectively. While less frequent than the creation of thallium or mercury, the results show that the LHC currently produces gold at a maximum rate of about 89 000 nuclei per second from lead–lead collisions at the ALICE collision point. Gold nuclei emerge from the collision with very high energy and hit the LHC beam pipe or collimators at various points downstream, where they immediately fragment into single protons, neutrons and other particles. The gold exists for just a tiny fraction of a second.
The ALICE analysis shows that, during Run 2 of the LHC (2015–2018), about 86 billion
gold nuclei were created at the four major experiments. In terms of mass, this corresponds to just 29 picograms (2.9 ×10
-11
g). Since the luminosity in the LHC is continually increasing thanks to regular upgrades to the machines, Run 3 has produced almost double the amount of gold that Run 2 did, but the total still amounts to trillions of times less than would be required to make a piece of jewellery. While the dream of medieval alchemists has technically come true, their hopes of riches have once again been dashed.
“Thanks to the unique capabilities of the ALICE ZDCs, the present analysis is the first to systematically detect and analyse the signature of gold production at the LHC experimentally,” says Uliana Dmitrieva of the ALICE collaboration.
“The results also test and improve theoretical models of electromagnetic dissociation which, beyond their intrinsic physics interest, are used to understand and predict beam losses that are a major limit on the performance of the LHC and future colliders,”

• **粒子加速器产生金元素的实际意义**：
  - [omnee] 提到在LHC中产生了微量的金元素，虽然量极少，但象征着炼金术梦想的实现。
  - [elashri] 通过计算表明，即使在理想条件下，LHC需要1850亿年才能产生足够支付未来环形对撞机（FCC）的金元素，暗示实际应用不现实。

• **技术进步的局限性**：
  - [cookingmyserver] 认为当前技术进步更多受限于资源和工程能力，而非知识。并指出在生物化学和生物学领域仍有大量未知，这些领域可能带来更多实用知识。
  - [dclowd9901] 对比了粒子加速器炼金与数字货币挖矿，认为后者更具经济效益，暗示当前技术应用的偏差。

• **炼金术的历史和文化关联**：
  - [John23832] 提出历史上的炼金师为何专注于将铅转变为金，而不是其他元素，质疑这可能与两者都是重金属有关。
  - [DrScientist] 开玩笑地暗示LHC的真实目的是实现物理学家炼金的梦想，提到牛顿也曾沉迷于炼金术。

• **未来科技对社会的影响**：
  - [tarkin2] 和 [comrade1234] 都提到了如果金元素的大量人工生产成为现实，可能对全球财富和经济体系产生巨大影响，类似于科幻小说的情节。
  - [725686] 感叹历史上炼金师的思想超前，虽然方法不同，但目标一致。

补充讨论：
• **核反应与其他元素转化**：
  - [billiam] 提到法国的核反应堆不仅用于发电，还通过核反应将铀转化为钚，暗示核反应在元素转化中的广泛应用。

争议焦点：
• **技术应用的实际性和优先级**：部分评论质疑通过粒子加速器产生金元素的实际意义和经济可行性，认为当前技术更应关注其他领域的突破。

data.title: Show HN: Hyper – Standards first React alternative
data.author: tipiirai
data.article_summary: Hyper是一种以标准为核心的标记语言，用于构建用户界面，强调使用HTML、CSS和JavaScript，追求简洁和可扩展性。与React的混合逻辑、结构和样式的单体架构不同，Hyper实现了React 2013年最初的愿景：一个无头视图层。Hyper通过语义HTML和少量类名实现复杂UI，如其表格组件仅需3.9KB的JS，而现代React需要91.3KB。Hyper的设计系统允许通过一个32行的CSS文件实现主题转换，避免了React中通过CSS-in-JS或Tailwind造成的紧耦合和大量维护工作。Hyper通过严格的分离关注点，实现真正的可重用组件和零样板代码，使应用在扩展时仍保持简单。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：前端开发框架的复杂性与功能取舍，以及不同技术方案的比较

不同观点：
• [rustc] 认为在“复杂组件”代码对比中，React 包含了更多的功能（如完整样式、图标、可排序列等），而 Nue 仅通过顶层元素的 "card" 类就自动实现了这些功能。他质疑 Nue 是否真的能如此简化开发，还是只是隐藏了复杂性。

• [vessenes] 对 Nue 这样的乌托邦式项目表示欣赏，但指出 React 提供了大量功能，其复杂性在一定程度上是合理的。他认为新框架如果要简化系统，就需要在功能上做出妥协。他还提到，React 处于功能-复杂性帕累托曲线上一个较高的位置，开发者需要决定是否为了简化而放弃一些功能。

• [nicce] 关注 Nue 如何解决类似 React Server Components 的问题，特别是消除前后端之间的网络实现差异，使组件可以同时在前后端定义并根据需要动态添加客户端功能。他认为这是评估新框架的一个关键点。

• [jitl] 提出了如何使用 Hyper 对包含 100,000 项的表格进行虚拟化渲染的问题，关注性能和可扩展性。

• [superchris] 认为 Nue 与 Sprae 很相似，并提到他使用 Sprae 连接模板和后端状态的实践。他提供了 Sprae 的使用案例，显示出对类似技术方案的兴趣。

• [tipiirai] 作为 Nue 的作者，阐明了该项目的设计目标：1. 优先使用标准技术（HTML、CSS、JavaScript）；2. 减少抽象，简化UI组合；3. 支持设计系统；4. 保证可扩展性，即使应用变复杂也能保持简单。

• [andrewmcwatters] 质疑为何要使用 Hyper，认为直接使用 web 标准和 web 组件技术已经足够，无需引入新的依赖。他提到他们的团队已经放弃了 React 等主流框架，以减少依赖和不必要的复杂性，并认为成熟软件项目应尽量减少依赖。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新框架如 Nue 是否真的能简化开发，还是只是将复杂性隐藏在了底层。
• 另一个讨论点是 React 等成熟框架的功能-复杂性平衡，以及开发者是否愿意为了简化而放弃一些功能。
• 还有对新框架如何处理前后端集成和性能优化（如虚拟化渲染）的关注。
• 一些开发者对直接使用 web 标准和减少依赖的趋势表示支持，反映出对简化开发流程的强烈需求。

43936844.article_content:
Hyper is a standards first markup language for building user interfaces. It enables developers (and AI models) to generate complex UIs with amazingly clean syntax.
Project goals
Standards first
: User interfaces should be assembled with HTML, styled with CSS, and enhanced with JavaScript.
Simplicity
: UI composition should be easy and require as few idioms and abstractions as possible, both on client and server (SSR).
Design Systems
: Design should be a separate subsystem, easily accessible for developers who care about and understand design.
Scalability
: Complex UIs should retain simplicity as the application grows.
To understand how these goals are met, we use React as a counter-example because it's the opposite of Hyper's architecture and design goals. React embraces a monolithic architecture where logic, structure, and styling are mixed together, while Hyper is what React 1.0 (2013) originally envisioned: just a headless view layer.
Let's study the difference in more detail:

In this example, we chose ShadCN as it's gained significant popularity in recent years and has strong AI tool support. For example, Claude and ChatGPT offer built-in support for ShadCN in their code previews.

Modern React: tightly coupled design
This kind of design swap becomes a large programming effort when design choices are coupled into components via CSS-in-JS or Tailwind. For example, in ShadCN, to change the typography of your headings, you need to edit

Tight coupling can also create a maintenance issue. For example, ShadCN's

additional TSX code
to maintain.
While you definitely
can
decouple your styling from your React components, this pattern is rarely seen in real-world applications. Instead, the use of vanilla CSS is often discouraged due to concerns about
global namespace pollution
or other reasons.
Hyper: decoupled design system

This solves three key issues in modern React:
Truly reusable components
across projects and styling contexts
Central design system
easily maintainable from the same place
Zero boilerplate
due to strict separation of concerns

data.title: 21 GB/s CSV Parsing Using SIMD on AMD 9950X
data.author: zigzag312
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Sep软件版本0.10.0的性能优化，特别是在AMD 9950X（Zen 5）处理器上使用AVX-512指令集实现了21 GB/s的CSV解析速度。与之前的18 GB/s相比，新版本通过绕过.NET 9.0中对AVX-512掩码寄存器处理的次优代码生成，实现了显著的性能提升。文章详细比较了从Sep 0.1.0到0.10.0的性能进展，展示了从早期的7 GB/s到最新21 GB/s的提升过程。同时，作者分析了AVX-512和AVX2在9950X上的表现，发现AVX2表现更优，进而开发了一个新的AVX-512-to-256解析器，进一步提升了性能。文章通过代码和汇编分析，展示了如何通过软件优化与硬件升级共同实现性能飞跃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Intel移除AVX-512支持以及对数据处理性能优化的技术讨论

不同观点：
• [chao-] 认为Intel移除消费者SKU中的AVX-512支持是不合理的。Intel花费多年时间推动AVX-512的应用，而当更多库开始使用它时，Intel却放弃了这一特性，反而让AMD在消费者CPU上支持AVX-512。

• [stabbles] 关注于数据处理中的具体技术优化，提出通过使用SIMD指令（如shuffle和ternary logic）可以显著减少操作次数，并提供了博客链接详细说明这一技巧。

• [winterbloom] 强调在短时间内（约两年）实现了约3倍的性能提升，但指出这种提升不能简单归因于单独的硬件升级。

• [Aardwolf] 批评Intel移除AVX-512支持的决定，暗示这是为了推广带有慢速核心的CPU架构，而不是考虑多泵架构（multi-pumping）。

• [voidUpdate] 对需要极高速处理CSV文件的应用场景表示质疑，暗示如此高的性能需求在实际应用中可能并不常见。

• [vessenes] 幽默地期待有人能超越当前性能优化，提出如果幸运的话，可能会看到Arthur Whitney发布更高效的解决方案。

• [criddell] 对使用C#而非汇编语言实现高性能数据处理表示赞赏，认为这是一个令人印象深刻的成果。

• [imtringued] 对CSV处理性能的基准测试提出质疑，认为CSV的非标准性质使得简单的字节吞吐量数据具有误导性，特别是当未考虑实际数据解析需求时。

• [zeristor] 提出使用Parquet这种更高效的数据存储格式，质疑为何在CSV上进行如此深度的性能优化。

补充讨论：
• 关于AVX-512的讨论中，焦点在于Intel放弃消费者SKU中的AVX-512支持是否合理，以及AMD在这一方面的策略优势。
• 数据处理性能优化方面，具体技术如shuffle和ternary logic的使用、基准测试的有效性以及不同数据格式的选择（如CSV vs. Parquet）都是讨论的热点。
• 对实际应用场景的需求和CSV格式本身的局限性也引发了进一步的思考和争议。

43936097.article_content:
Aberdeen
Build blazing-fast, declarative UIs in pure TypeScript/JavaScript – no virtual DOM.
Aberdeen offers a refreshingly simple approach to reactive UIs. Its core idea:
Use many small, anonymous functions for emitting DOM elements, and automatically rerun them when their underlying
proxied
data changes. This proxied data can be anything from simple values to complex, typed, and deeply nested data structures.
Now, let's dive into why this matters...
Why use Aberdeen?
🎩
Elegant and simple:
Express UIs naturally in JavaScript/TypeScript, without complex abstractions, build steps, or JSX. No hooks, no
setState
, no lifting state, no state management libraries. Just proxied data and automatically rerunning functions.
⏩
Fast:
No virtual DOM. Aberdeen intelligently updates only the minimal, necessary parts of your UI when proxied data changes.
👥
Awesome lists
: It's very easy and performant to reactively display data sorted by whatever you like.
🔬
Tiny:
Around 5KB (minimized and gzipped) and with zero runtime dependencies.
🔋
Batteries included
: Comes with client-side routing, revertible patches for optimistic user-interface updates, component-local CSS, helper functions for transforming reactive data (mapping, partitioning, filtering, etc) and hide/unhide transition effects. No bikeshedding required!
Why
not
use Aberdeen?
🤷
Lack of community:
There are not many of us -Aberdeen developers- yet, so don't expect terribly helpful Stack Overflow/AI answers.
📚
Lack of ecosystem:
You'd have to code things yourself, instead of duct-taping together a gazillion React ecosystem libraries.
Examples

data.title: Itter.sh – Micro-Blogging via Terminal
data.author: rrr_oh_man
data.article_summary:
**itter.sh** 是一个通过 **SSH** 访问的微型博客平台，旨在提供无干扰的社交体验。用户通过终端操作，每次发布最多180字符的内容（称为"eets"），支持标签和提及。平台无浏览器和算法推送，强调简洁和高效。

**主要功能：**
1. **注册与登录**：通过 SSH 命令注册和登录。
2. **发布与互动**：使用命令发布 eets、查看时间线、关注用户等。
3. **账户管理**：编辑个人资料、查看帮助、清除屏幕等。

**技术栈**：基于 Python、AsyncSSH 和 Supabase 构建，主打怀旧终端体验。

• **zipping1549**：提到另一个相关项目（bbj-dev/bbj），为讨论提供了更多技术选择。
• **flaviuspopan**：对项目表示赞赏，特别提到了名字、logo和“bugs”部分，但提到遇到了执行请求失败的问题。

43936884.article_summary:
**itter.sh** 是一个通过 **SSH** 访问的微型博客平台，旨在提供无干扰的社交体验。用户通过终端操作，每次发布最多180字符的内容（称为"eets"），支持标签和提及。平台无浏览器和算法推送，强调简洁和高效。

**主要功能：**
1. **注册与登录**：通过 SSH 命令注册和登录。
2. **发布与互动**：使用命令发布 eets、查看时间线、关注用户等。
3. **账户管理**：编辑个人资料、查看帮助、清除屏幕等。

**技术栈**：基于 Python、AsyncSSH 和 Supabase 构建，主打怀旧终端体验。
43936884.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个基于终端界面（SSH/Telnet）的项目及其概念的评价和讨论

不同观点：
• **csomar**：认为SSH输入延迟影响体验，尤其是在需要通过打字导航界面时。尽管如此，仍然喜欢这个概念，倾向于使用终端流而不是网页导航。
• **ramaro**：提供了一个相关的替代项目链接（pico.sh），但没有详细评价。
• **tehlike**：对构建类似终端应用程序感兴趣，正在为自己的项目（pricetracker.wtf）寻找相关技术方案，并提到已经发现了一些有用的库。
• **zipping1549**：提到另一个相关项目（bbj-dev/bbj），为讨论提供了更多技术选择。
• **flaviuspopan**：对项目表示赞赏，特别提到了名字、logo和“bugs”部分，但提到遇到了执行请求失败的问题。
• **ilvez**：对项目实现时间表示好奇，认为缺少readline支持，并提到最初以为可以直接从命令行使用。
• **joshcsimmons**：对项目概念表示强烈支持，认为这种避开现代网页广告噪音的导航方式非常棒，并询问了项目的采用情况。
• **alexrsagen**：遇到了用户未找到的错误，无法正常使用项目。
• **thunkle**：对项目自贬式的幽默（大量bug）表示欣赏。
• **abhisek**：认为项目让人想起BBS时代，暗示一种怀旧情感。
• **codingdave**：对“微型博客”的存在提出质疑，认为这种形式源于早期短信的限制，不理解为何要在一个新工具中引入过时的限制。

补充讨论：
• 项目的核心概念引发了对终端界面体验的广泛讨论，有人支持其避开现代网页复杂性的做法，有人则关注具体的技术问题和功能缺失。
• 争议焦点之一是项目中“微型博客”功能的价值，codingdave对此提出质疑，认为这种形式已经过时。
• 另一个值得注意的点是项目中遇到的技术问题，如SSH输入延迟、执行请求失败和用户未找到等错误，显示出项目在实际应用中的挑战。
• 项目引发的怀旧情感也是一个讨论亮点，abhisek提到它让人想起BBS时代。

data.title: Hollow Core Fiber (HCF)
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: Hollow Core Fiber (HCF)是一种通过中空核心传输光信号的光纤，与传统实心玻璃或塑料核心的光纤不同。HCF的中心是空心，通常充满空气或真空，外部由特殊结构的包层包围，利用光子带隙或反共振效应引导光传输。与传统光纤相比，HCF具有更低的信号衰减，因为光在空气或真空中传输时，吸收和散射损耗更小。此外，HCF还具有更低的延迟，因为光在空气中的传播速度快于实心材料，适用于高频交易和实时通信等需要高速的应用。同时，HCF能够承受更高的功率，减少非线性效应和材料损伤风险。HCF在数据传输效率和性能方面具有显著优势，有望革新光纤通信领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： hollow-core optical fibers（空心光纤）的技术进展及其应用前景

不同观点：
• GlibMonkeyDeath：最初认为空心光纤由于高衰减限制了其在长距离通信中的应用，仅适用于短距离和特殊需求（如超高功率传输、低色散、低非线性等）。但通过查阅最新资料，发现该技术在实验室环境中已经实现了与传统单模石英光纤相当的损耗水平，认为这是一个惊人的进展，并对未来应用持积极态度。

• ksec：对空心光纤的未来持乐观态度，提到其有可能在减少延迟方面发挥重要作用（如减少日本到纽约的通信延迟约50毫秒）。然而，认为目前该技术的实际应用还远未达到预期。

• exabrial：从工程角度出发，关注空心光纤在实际应用中的技术挑战，包括如何在拼接时不压坏纤芯，如何在拼接和维护真空环境，以及如何进行终端处理。

• sunrunner：对文章链接的URL感到不安，虽然未具体说明原因，但表达了对链接本身的不信任感。

• epx：对空心光纤拼接的难度表示好奇，关注技术实现中的具体问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的焦点包括空心光纤的损耗问题、实际应用中的技术挑战以及其在长距离通信中的潜力。
• GlibMonkeyDeath提供的最新论文链接（https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/470034/1/OFC2022_PD_Jasion_submi...）显示了实验室中的进展，这为空心光纤的未来应用带来了希望。
• ksec引用的两个链接（[1] https://www.laserfocusworld.com/fiber-optics/article/1417001... 和 [2] https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=16194973）进一步讨论了空心光纤的潜力和历史讨论。

争议焦点：
• 空心光纤在实际应用中面临的技术挑战（如拼接、终端处理、真空维护等）与其在实验室中取得的进展之间的差距，是讨论的主要争议点。尽管实验室中取得了重要进展，但实际应用中仍存在诸多未解决的问题。

What is Hollow Core Fiber (HCF)？
Holight Team

In the rapidly evolving field of
fiber optics
, one innovation stands out for its potential to revolutionize how we transmit data: hollow core fiber. Traditional optical fibers, which have been the backbone of telecommunications for decades, guide light through a solid glass or plastic core. However, hollow core fibers offer a groundbreaking alternative by channeling light through a hollow core, typically filled with air or vacuum. This unique design minimizes signal loss and dispersion, promising faster and more efficient data transmission.
But what exactly is hollow core fiber, and why is it generating so much excitement? In this post, we’ll delve into the basics of hollow core fiber technology, exploring how it works, its advantages over traditional fibers, and its potential applications. Whether you’re a tech enthusiast, a telecommunications professional, or just curious about the latest advancements in fiber optics, this comprehensive guide will provide you with everything you need to know about hollow core fiber.
What is Hollow Core Fiber？
Hollow core fiber is a type of optical fiber that guides light through a hollow central core, as opposed to the solid glass or plastic core used in traditional optical fibers. This innovative design leverages a central air or vacuum-filled core surrounded by a structured cladding that uses photonic bandgap or anti-resonant guiding mechanisms to confine and transmit light.
Key Components:
Core:
The central hollow region where light is transmitted. This core can be filled with air, vacuum, or sometimes other gases, depending on the application and design requirements.
Cladding:
Surrounds the hollow core and is engineered to guide light through the core using photonic bandgap effects or anti-resonant reflecting mechanisms. The cladding is typically made of high-purity silica with a periodic structure that creates the necessary optical properties.
Protective Layers:
Just like traditional optical fibers, hollow core fibers have protective coatings and buffer layers that protect the delicate internal structures from environmental damage, mechanical stress, and handling. These layers ensure the fiber’s durability and longevity in practical applications.
How It Differs from Traditional Solid Core Fiber
Light Propagation:
Solid Core Fiber: In traditional optical fibers, light is guided through a solid core made of glass or plastic by total internal reflection. The light travels through the material of the core, which can lead to attenuation (signal loss) due to absorption and scattering.
Hollow Core Fiber: In hollow core fibers, light is guided through a hollow core primarily by photonic bandgap effects or anti-resonant reflecting mechanisms. The light travels mostly through air or vacuum, which significantly reduces attenuation because air has lower absorption and scattering losses compared to solid materials.
Materials:
Solid Core Fiber: Typically made from high-purity silica glass or plastic.
Hollow Core Fiber: Constructed using a combination of silica glass and air or vacuum in the core.
Performance:
Solid Core Fiber: Suitable for a wide range of applications but can suffer from higher latency, higher non-linear effects, and higher dispersion.
Hollow Core Fiber: Offers lower latency, reduced non-linear effects, and lower dispersion, making it advantageous for specific high-performance applications.
Advantages of Hollow Core Fiber
Reduced Signal Loss
Hollow core fibers exhibit significantly lower attenuation compared to traditional solid core fibers because the majority of light transmission occurs through air or vacuum within the hollow core, rather than through a solid material. Air and vacuum have much lower absorption and scattering losses compared to silica or plastic, which are typically used in solid core fibers. This reduction in interaction with the core material minimizes signal degradation, allowing data to travel longer distances with less signal loss.
Lower Latency
Latency refers to the time it takes for data to travel from one point to another. Light travels faster in air (or vacuum) than it does in solid glass or plastic due to the lower refractive index of air. In hollow core fibers, the primary medium for light propagation is air, which significantly reduces the travel time for light pulses. Consequently, data transmission through hollow core fibers experiences lower latency, making these fibers particularly advantageous for applications where speed is critical, such as high-frequency trading and real-time communications.
Higher Power Handling
Hollow core fibers can handle higher power levels more effectively than solid core fibers. In solid core fibers, high-power light can cause nonlinear effects and potential damage to the core material. data.title: A Taxonomy for Rendering Engines
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了实时渲染引擎的分类体系，强调了分享行业内“来之不易”的经验教训的重要性。作者指出，游戏开发和计算机图形学领域虽然乐于分享技术进步，但往往忽视了幕后决策的讨论。文章呼吁建立一个描述渲染引擎背景的分类法，类似于数据库领域的成熟分类。作者提出了一个3x3维度分类框架，包括产品特性、生产过程和技术要求等方面，如引擎用户、平台支持、内容抽象、迭代速度、延迟处理、数据流等。文章最后强调，技术成功与用户规模和团队规模密切相关，解决工程问题需要考虑这些因素的复杂性。

主要讨论点：对当前行业发展状态以及技术工具选择的看法

不同观点：
• [munificent] 认为当前行业仍然很年轻，从业者往往过于关注新颖、吸引眼球的技术（如光照算法），而可能忽视其他更基础或实际的方面。这一观点暗示了对行业内技术追求方向的反思。

• [bluescrn] 则指出，截至2025年，行业中可能已经趋于使用统一的工具，例如UE5（虚幻引擎5），表明技术选择已经相对成熟和固定，没有太多其他选择。这暗示了对技术多样性减少的接受，以及对UE5的认可。

补充讨论：
• [munificent] 的评论反映出对行业技术追求方向的批评，认为从业者可能过度关注前沿技术，而不是更实用的解决方案。

• [bluescrn] 的评论则显示出对技术工具统一趋势的认可，认为UE5可能已经成为行业标准，不存在显著的其他选择。

• 争议的焦点在于对技术发展方向的看法：一方认为行业过度追求新技术，另一方认为技术已经相对成熟并趋于统一。

• 两者都承认行业在技术上已经取得了一定进展，但对如何选择和关注技术发展方向有不同见解。

43908220.article_content:
A Taxonomy for Rendering Engines.
Non-trivial problems are solved only in context.
It's time to grow up.
One of the main objectives behind the
REAC
conference we (Steve, Stephanie, Natalya, Michael and I) organize now every year is to share the kind of "hard won" lessons on the craft of real-time rendering that are currently not possible to learn outside working in our industry for decades (and possibly, on many different projects and companies...).
Gamedevs and Computer Graphics people are a great community, we do share a lot when it comes to how things are made, we are proud of pushing the state of the art forward and we want others to know about it! It's undeniable that without this openness, we would not be able to produce the incredible technology we have today. But, in many ways, we are still a young industry, we love to talk about shiny things, not as much the "less glamorous" behind the scene decisions that most often make all of the difference.
And because we are not used to doing this, we are not great at it! I was talking with someone (I'll ask them later if they want to appear by name) a few days ago about how they "hate" architecture talks, as most often are just showing how a given thing works - whilst not providing with the kind of context useful to evaluate if that solution would be good to consider.
I fully agree! I think it will take us, as an industry, some time to understand how to best present these lessons. It's the difference between a lazy post about the "10 habits of successful CEOs" and an academic text that tries to develop a theory of management.
Theories require assumptions, context, they need to be replicable, falsifiable.
A good start would be to develop a taxonomy of real-time rendering engines. A language to describe the context.
This is... normal, in all mature technologies. Let's think for example about
databases
. Nobody would say "this is how you make a database", that's such a vague statement. What kind of database? Relational, key-value, time-series, vector, graph, spatial, columnar? With what characteristics? Concurrent reads, writes or both? Distributed? Consistent? Persistent (durable)? Transactional? From the set of high-level use-cases and technological requirements we then can talk about algorithms and data structures, architectures - develop a theory and practice.
Perhaps we also were spoiled by the relative simplicity of graphics-related objectives. The rendering equation, in the rush towards photorealism, provided a simple, objective metric of progress we could compare to. And for the rest, more objects, more polygons, more textures, per unit of memory and time - was a good universal proxy of what we wanted to achieve. The tight loops that power our GPUs are relatively simpler to talk about than the remaining 90% of the engine around them.
A(n example) taxonomy: 3x3 dimensions.
Here are a few dimensions we might want to consider:
1) Product characteristics.
- Engine users. From narrow to widest: Single team proprietary, Multiple teams, Single-genre middleware, Multi-genre middleware, User-Generated Content platform.
- Platform support. Single-platform (e.g. web, or PlayStation), Multi-platform, Multimodal (Computers, Mobiles, Consoles, Web, Cars, VR...)
- Scalability needs. Is it a goal to target primarily a small set of devices with roughly comparable capabilities, or is the engine made to scale? Scale content down (level of detail), up (procedural detail generation) or both?
2) Production: people & process.
- Content abstraction. Is the engine an API for ad-hoc rendering code (i.e. no content pipelines, engine is a draw abstraction), or is it data-driven? If the latter, is the data "generic" (arbitrary mesh attributes with shaders / shadergraphs) or must it adhere to narrow schemas (specialized/"hardcoded" rendering loops per schema type)?
- Iteration. Does the engine prioritize live editing of its data (no baking - common for UGC as well) or is it made for "baking"? How long does it take from change to review?
- Users. Who is the engine made for? Artist-driven or Engineering-driven production? Does the engine target experts or is it meant to be easy to use?
3) Technological requirements.
- Latency. Can data be double and triple buffered to aid parallelism, or do we need to execute as eagerly as possible?
- Dynamics. What data do we constrain to remain static, and what is allowed to change?
- Streaming. None (in-core rendering), local (disk-to-memory), distributed (cloud/server to client).
The tenth dimension.
...is success (or scale). This is arguably the most important one, but I consider this to be true for software engineering in general - not something specific about 3d rendering.
Technology with no users is
(mostly)
trivial
. Engineering problems scale exponentially with the number of users of a product, both current and total during its historical development. And similarly, with the team size needed to develop said product.

data.title: NSF faces shake-up as officials abolish its 37 divisions
data.author: magicalist
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国科学研究资金和学术界的未来不确定性及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **ddahlen**：基于个人在学术界和工业界的经验，指出目前学术界的不确定性，包括招聘冻结、国际研究生面临离境压力、科研人员资金被削减等问题。特别提到政府资助的战略性投资对于保持关键知识的重要性，尤其是在私营企业可能倒闭的情况下。
  
• **ourmandave**：关注新的资助提案审查流程，特别是与多元化、公平和包容（DEI）相关的新标准。批评这种新结构可能会导致不符合"总统指令"的提案被否决，暗示这种做法是出于政治动机。

• **frob**：个人经历显示NSF资助对其成长的重要性，认为目前的政策变化正在破坏这些帮助科研人员发展的机制。

• **hdivider**：质疑是否会利用机器学习系统进行更集中的审查，并担心政府通过这种方式加强对资金分配的控制。同时指出当前系统的演变是为了防止滥用，但新的集权化操作可能会带来问题。

• **chairhairair**：从预算角度出发，指出NSF的预算相对较少，质疑政府为何关注科学领域的调整而不是其他更大预算的部门。

• **adamc**：简单表达对美国科学领域遭受损害的担忧。

• **insane_dreamer**：认为削减科研经费将严重损害美国的全球竞争力，并预测这种损害可能需要十年或更长时间才能恢复，即使未来政策回调。

• **xhkkffbf**：提出特朗普政府的政策是对拜登时期将大量资金分配给特定种族和性别群体的反动，认为这是政治化的结果，并指出这种做法引起了科学界的嫉妒和实际问题。

• **antonvs**：认为特朗普政府的核心动机是摧毁曾经让他感到羞辱的系统，指出这种破坏性行为的根源是个人屈辱和潜在的无意识目标。

• **fabian2k**：指出预算削减高达55%，不仅仅是重组，而是对科研系统的实质性破坏，并认为剩余部分还将被迫 adher 一种意识形态纯净的"反觉醒"路线。

• **srikanth767**：简短地暗示目前的政策可能是某种贿赂机制。

• **SubiculumCode**：强烈反对NSF和NIH的预算削减，认为这将严重损害美国的国际地位，并指出科学家可能会因此迁移到欧洲和加拿大。

• **ThinkBeat**：从法律角度出发，指出预算需要国会批准，质疑特朗普政府是否可以直接决定最终预算。

• **superkuh**：提供一个绕过Cloudflare的存档链接，以方便访问被限制的文章。

• **LightBug1**：以旁观者身份表达对美国现状的讽刺和无奈，认为美国民主制度已经做出了选择，美国需要承担这种后果。

补充讨论：
- 讨论的焦点包括科研经费削减的潜在影响、资助审查流程的政治化倾向、对学术和科研系统未来不确定性的担忧，以及对美国全球竞争力的长远影响。
- 不同评论者对当前政策变化的动机有不同的看法，一些人认为是出于政治动机，另一些人则认为是对过去政策的不满和反动。
- 对科研系统恢复能力的讨论也较为突出，部分评论者认为即使未来政策调整，恢复科研能力也需要很长时间。

data.title: CryptPad: An Alternative to the Google Suite
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: CryptPad是一款注重隐私的协作办公套件，提供端到端加密，开源且支持实时编辑与协作。用户无需账户即可共享文件夹和文件，数据无法追溯到创建者，且不含追踪功能。相比Google Docs，CryptPad在保证隐私的同时不牺牲功能和易用性，支持多操作系统，具备简洁的界面和丰富的应用，如富文本编辑器、Kanban工具等。用户赞赏其安全性、开放源代码、零知识加密以及无需电子邮件地址注册的便利性，适用于学校、工作场所等多场景的文档协作。CryptPad免费且匿名，被视为Google Drive的隐私友好替代品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Cryptpad及其相关加密文档工具的功能、安全性、兼容性及用户体验的评价和争议。

不同观点：
• Aaravchen认为Cryptpad不仅提供了加密云存储，还积极填补了工具上的空白，比如支持markdown文件，方便快速记录简单笔记，而无需创建完整文档。

• Righthand则指出Cryptpad将用户锁定在其平台内，若要提取文档，必须使用其UI进行解密。他更倾向于使用Syncthing来处理同步和加密，以获得更高的自主性。

• Hmsimha提出Cryptpad存在安全漏洞，尤其是通过分享链接分享的文档可能被Google、Apple、Microsoft等大公司获取。他还指出Cryptpad未能防范某些攻击，如服务器被攻破或恶意浏览器扩展导致文档泄露。尽管Cryptpad提供了额外的密码保护，但这不是默认设置，实际使用中很少人会启用。

• Weinzierl提供信息，指出有多个免费的Cryptpad实例可用，例如cryptpad.digitalcourage.de，并建议查看cryptpad.org/instances获取更多实例。

• Ocdtrekkie的主要不满在于Cryptpad的加载时间过长，尤其是当文档是公开分享时，这种长时间加载显得不合理。

• Mupuff1234质疑Cryptpad被称作Google Suite的替代品而非Microsoft Suite，并指出其使用了Microsoft的图标，感到困惑。

• Dbbk简单批评Cryptpad的界面设计过时，看起来像是90年代的风格。

补充讨论：
• Cryptpad的安全性和隐私保护是争议的焦点，尤其是分享链接可能导致文档被大公司获取的问题。
• 用户对Cryptpad的性能（如加载时间）和界面设计存在不满。
• 不同用户对Cryptpad的功能和兼容性有不同期望，比如与Syncthing的集成和默认安全设置的改进。
• 有人对Cryptpad的品牌定位和视觉设计提出质疑。

data.title: Dasung Paperlike 13K is a 13.3 inch E Ink color monitor
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: Dasung Paperlike 13K是一款13.3英寸的E Ink彩色显示器，分辨率为3200x2400像素，灰度内容显示可达300ppi，刷新率最高37Hz。该显示器支持USB Type-C和HDMI输入，具备触屏和反向触控功能，可连接安卓手机进行屏幕镜像。它有一个3.5毫米耳机插孔、内置扬声器和DC电源输入，配有六个物理按钮用于调节功能。机身由铝合金制成，重721克，支持VESA安装。彩色版售价749美元，黑白版售价679美元，目前已开始预售。彩色版配有前光，而黑白版没有。该显示器不完全支持苹果设备，主要兼容Windows、Linux和Android系统。预计2025年5月发货。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：彩色电子墨水屏设备、预购和价格问题、使用场景和目标市场、技术参数和性能

不同观点：
• **对预购和客服的不满**：greysonp提到预购了25"显示器但未收到货，尽管多次联系客服仍未解决，建议远离该品牌。
• **寻找适合的阅读设备**：outlore询问是否有适合阅读教科书的平板尺寸、轻量级电子阅读器，不希望有严重的厂商锁定，正在考虑Boox、Kindle Scribe或iPad。
• **质疑视频真实性**：twiclo对视频中的刷新率表示怀疑，认为可能作假。
• **讨论价格构成**：comrade1234提到Dasung在中国和墨西哥生产，质疑从中国和墨西哥进口产品的价格和关税差异。
• **对价格差异的疑惑**：Pet_Ant对彩色版只比黑白版贵70美元表示惊讶，猜测可能有DPI或耐用性等方面的显著差异。

补充讨论：
• **使用场景的质疑**：neves质疑这种设备的主要用途是否仅限于阅读漫画。zeeveener则表示不理解这种产品的目标市场，认为彩色电子阅读器是噱头，且不适合日常使用或作为显示器。
• **替代选择和性价比**：lnyan提到预购了更便宜的Bigme 13英寸彩色电子墨水显示器，价格为499美元，但可能质量和算法不如Dasung。gitroom对新硬件持谨慎态度，质疑这些小众屏幕是否会真正流行或只是早期用户的 hype。
• **其他技术选项**：bismark询问是否有人尝试过Eazeye RLCD显示器，表示对眼疲劳的技术进步感到兴奋。silvestrov关心价格和功耗问题，并考虑这种显示器是否适合制造超轻便携设备。
• **对尺寸的偏好**：xtiansimon对13.3英寸或全尺寸8.5x11的格式表示赞赏。
• **兼容性问题**：mrinfinite指出某些25.3英寸屏幕不兼容Mac，这对Mac用户来说是个问题。

The
Dasung Paperlike 13K
is a monitor with a 13.3 inch, 3200 x 2400 pixel E Ink color display that can show grayscale content at 300 pixels per inch with screen refresh rates as high as 37 Hz, although those numbers will drop if you want to view color content or emphasize image quality.
Dasung first announced
earlier this month
, and now the company has
begun taking pre-orders for $749
. There’s also a preview page for an
upcoming Indieogogo campaign
. There’s also a
black-and-white only model that sells for $679
.
The monitor supports USB Type-C and HDMI input and it has a touchscreen and “reverse touch control functionality.” Basically that means that if you plug in an Android phone or another supported device, you should be able to mirror your screen to the monitor and interact with the apps on your phone by touching the monitor.
There’s also a 3.5mm audio jack, a built-in speaker, and a DC power input, along with six physical buttons along one side for power, brightness, contrast, and other functions.
Dasung’s Paperlike 13K has an aluminum alloy body that measures 307 x 241 x 5mm (at its thinnest point) and weighs 721 grams. Dasung doesn’t say how thick the display is at its
thickest
point, but images suggest it’s about twice as thick at the base as it is at the top.
The monitor comes with several accessories including HDMI and USB-C cables, as well as two different stand options. One is a “portable stand stick” that’s pretty much a pen-sized stick that screws into a hole on the back of the monitor, allowing you to prop it up on the go. The other is a magnetic protective cover that serves as a folio case that wraps around the front and back of the display for easy transport, but which can also be folded for use as a stand.
There are also a set of magnetic nuts included in the box that allow you to connect the display to a VESA mount.
A few other things to note:
Dasung only mentions the 300 ppi display resolution for this monitor, but the company is most likely using an E Ink Kaleido 3 display which means that the pixel density will drop to 150 ppi for color content.
E Ink’s Kaleido 3 displays support up to 4096 colors, can be viewed using only ambient light (with no backlight or front light required), and consume very little power because they only need to use electricity when the content on the page is refreshed.
But colors look muted compared with LCD or AMOLED displays, Kaleido screens are typically a little darker than black and white E Ink displays, and while you
can
push screen refresh rates high enough for smooth scrolling, video, and other animations, this typically comes at the cost of visual clarity. So you may notice some ghosting unless you stick to lower refresh rates or occasionally force a full screen refresh.
The color version of this portable monitor does have a front light, but the black and white version does not. So you may want to either count on using it in a well-lit room or investing in a clip-on book light.
The Paperlike 13K doesn’t fully support Apple devices including Macs, iPhones, or iPads yet. Windows, Linux, and Android are.
Orders placed now should ship “in about 3 weeks,” suggesting that we can expect them to ship in mid to late May, 2025.

data.title: Structuring Competency-Based Courses Through Skill Trees
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过技能树（Skill Trees）结构化基于能力课程的新方法，特别适用于计算机科学教育。随着教育向能力导向和自动化教学发展，现有的以理论为中心的课程结构不再适用。技能树展示了技能之间的依赖关系，并结合概念树（Concept Trees）来包含直观的概念或抽象模型。该框架提供了技能树和概念树的正式定义，并给出了设计和课程规划指南。在一个大学数据库课程中的应用显示，学生困惑和压力减少，达到预期技能水平所需的学习时间缩短。本文已提交至Koli Calling '25会议发表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技能树学习方法的有效性及其应用

不同观点：
• Garlef认为，将复合技能分解为子技能的学习方式存在误区。他提出两点论据：1) 掌握子技能A和B并不意味着能自动结合使用；2) 掌握复合技能并不意味着能单独执行其中的子技能。他以学习音乐为例，说明即便学会了音乐片段A和B，仍需练习过渡部分，且即便掌握了复合部分，单独演奏B也可能有困难。

• didgeoridoo提到Exercism.org使用了类似的学习方法，但对其背后的教育学驱动或趣味性和进度感的作用表示疑问，并提出哪些知识领域不易用这种方法结构化的问题。

• cultofmetatron支持这种学习方法，认为其有效，尤其是在mathacademy中的应用，并希望更多MOOCs采用这种教学模式。

• roenxi认为这种方法在软件工程管理中可能更具应用价值，尤其是在解决管理能力评估危机方面，提出通过技能树进行能力培训和测试的潜在优势。

• johnecheck支持将技能树模型用于小规模学习与职业培训，认为这种方法能为学习者提供清晰的指导地图，并指出大学在大规模教育中已采用类似方法。

• whiteborb指出这种方法面临的挑战，即需要定义和列举“技能”，而现实世界中的技能往往需要灵活组合工具和策略。但他认为这一挑战并非不可克服，并提到LLMs可能有助于创造新场景。

• accrual表示这种方法很有道理，并希望高等教育能采用，同时提及考虑攻读乔治亚理工学院的在线MSc学位，质疑其是否采用这种技能树方法。

• johnsutor赞同这种方法，并提到mathacademy.com的类似应用。

补充讨论：
• pyinstallwoes提到这种方法让他想起SWG（Star Wars Galaxies）游戏中的技能树，暗示其在游戏中的应用。

• rahimnathwani提到PDF引用了Justin关于Math Academy的书，并建议使用LLM提示生成技能树，例如为写一部魔幻现实主义小说创建技能树，并转化为mermaid代码。

争议焦点：
• Garlef对技能分解和复合技能学习的质疑与其他支持者（如cultofmetatron和roenxi）的观点形成对比，反映出对这种方法实际应用效果的不同看法。

Computer Science > Computers and Society

[Submitted on 23 Apr 2025]
Title:
Structuring Competency-Based Courses Through Skill Trees
Authors:
Hildo Bijl
View a PDF of the paper titled Structuring Competency-Based Courses Through Skill Trees, by Hildo Bijl
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Computer science education has seen two important trends. One has been a shift from raw theory towards skills: competency-based teaching. Another has been increasing student numbers, with as a result more automation in teaching. When automating education, it is crucial to properly structure courses, both to manage digitalized educational resources and to facilitate automated coaching algorithms. Currently existing structuring methodologies are focused around theory and not around skills, and are incapable of modeling the dependency links between skills. Because of this, a new didactic framework is needed.
This paper presents a new method of structuring educational contents around skills: something that a student is expected to be able to do. It defines Skill Trees that show dependencies between skills, and subsequently couples these to Concept Trees that contain intuitive ideas/notional machines. Due to the algorithmic nature of computer science, this step-wise approach is especially well-suited to this field of education. Next to formal definitions on Skill Trees and Concept Trees, guidelines are given on how to design them and how to plan a course using them.
The Skill Trees framework has been applied to improve the structure of a university database course. Student interviews indicated reduced confusion/stress and less study time required for students to meet their desired skill level.

data.title: Entire BART system is down due to computer systems failure
data.author: ksajadi
data.article_summary: BART服务因电脑网络问题全面暂停，建议乘客选择其他交通方式。Embarcadero站新电梯启用，BART董事会因PG&E停电改至下午1点召开。BART将为2025年Bay to Breakers提供特别早班服务，且在第一季度暴力犯罪率下降23%。2025年初湾区公共交通客流量显著增加。乘客可使用BART行程规划器查看实时信息和站台详情。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BART系统全线停运事件及其背后的原因和影响

不同观点：
• [技术猜测] 一些用户如scarmig和whalesalad猜测停运可能与DNS问题或其他计算机网络问题有关，尽管具体原因尚不明确。scarmig特别提到可能并非网络攻击。
• [财政与管理问题] fhkatari和ashayh认为BART面临的挑战部分源于其对票务收入的依赖，而非政府补贴，导致疫情期间乘客减少对系统打击严重。ashayh进一步批评美国在公共交通上的投资不足，反而花费巨资在AI等领域。
• [系统可靠性与改进] neilv和CoffeeOnWrite关注BART系统的可靠性和改进潜力。neilv质疑是否会有事后分析和技术改进以增强系统韧性。CoffeeOnWrite则对新闸机扫描器的故障及其对乘客的影响表示不满，质疑媒体为何未对此进行报道。

补充讨论：
• [个人经历与替代方案] a_t48分享了BART停运后的替代交通方式，认为乘坐 ferry 和F线虽然多花时间但避开了交通拥堵。ujkhsjkdhf234和satiated_grue则对比欧洲和美国交通系统，表达了对美国交通系统表现的不满。
• [幽默与讽刺] quotemstr和notpushkin以幽默和讽刺的方式讨论事件，quotemstr开玩笑地问是否用完了5.25英寸软盘，notpushkin则提到这可能成为一个有趣的动漫情节。
• [最新动态] throwaway81523提供了系统恢复但有严重延误的最新信息，并附上新闻链接。noitpmeder提到BART总部昨日停电，可能与事件有关。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在BART系统技术故障的原因及管理问题，特别是对新设备故障和乘客影响的处理方式不满，以及对美国公共交通投资优先级的批评。

data.title: USPTO refuses Tesla Robotaxi trademark as "merely descriptive"
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 特斯拉计划推出一款售价低于3万美元的无人驾驶双座车，但其商标申请遇阻。美国专利商标局（USPTO）拒绝特斯拉注册“robotaxi”商标，认为该词过于通用，且已有其他公司使用类似名称。此外，特斯拉申请的“Cybercab”商标也被拒，因与其他已注册商标存在潜在混淆。特斯拉必须为车辆寻找新名称，且面临技术挑战，如其自动驾驶系统频需人工干预。特斯拉计划在德州奥斯汀部署这些车辆，但不配备方向盘，将依赖远程操作处理复杂问题。此事还涉及与电影《银翼杀手2049》相关的商标纠纷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tesla的自动驾驶技术、商标以及与机器人出租车（robo taxi）市场的关系

不同观点：
• [geodel & drcongo] 对Tesla及其创始人尝试影响美国专利商标局（USPTO）的讽刺态度。geodel暗示Tesla可能会试图关闭USPTO，而drcongo则进一步夸大认为USPTO会在一周内被瓦解。

• [tim333 & JohnTHaller] 讨论了Tesla的全自动驾驶（FSD）技术的现状。tim333引用了Tesla FSD社区跟踪器的数据，指出每206英里的城市驾驶会出现一次关键性脱离（disengagement），并戏称可能应叫“Tesla Robocrash”。JohnTHaller补充说明“Robotaxi”这个名称在科幻小说中已经使用了数十年，质疑Tesla的商标命名。

• [connicpu & charlieo88] 讨论了Tesla商标的合理性。connicpu认为Tesla可以使用“Tesla™ Robotaxi”这个名称，因为已经拥有商标，且“Robotaxi”部分仅是描述性的。charlieo88则幽默地建议使用“Johnny Cab”（1990年施瓦辛格电影中的机器人出租车名称），质疑为何Tesla没有选择一个更有创意的名字。

• [mchusma & bilsbie] 对商标决定表示支持。mchusma认为这是一个理智的知识产权决定，而bilsbie尽管自称是Tesla的狂热支持者，但也认为这一决定是公平的。

• [lupusreal] 对Tesla选择“taxi”一词表示质疑。lupusreal认为Tesla使用“taxi”一词可能会削弱其市场 hype，因为这相当于承认其目标是利润率低、地理限制和市场利基的出租车行业，且即便完全占领全球出租车市场，也无法支撑其当前的市值，暗示投资者对Tesla的期望是不现实的。

补充讨论：
• [pupppet] 以幽默方式回应，暗示只需一个电话即可解决问题，可能是对Tesla创始人Elon Musk影响力的讽刺。

争议焦点：
• Tesla使用“Robotaxi”名称是否合适，特别是在科幻作品中已经使用数十年的情况下。
• Tesla是否应将其市场目标定位于利润率较低的出租车行业，以及这是否与其当前市值和投资者期望相符。

"We are an AI, robotics company," Tesla CEO Elon Musk
announced last April
. Despite the fact that the company's revenues are
overwhelmingly derived from selling new electric vehicles
, such prosaic activities hold no luster for the boss.
Instead, Tesla's future, according to Musk, depends upon a (claimed) sub-$30,000 driverless two-seater,
revealed to the world last October
in a staged demonstration on a film set.
But Musk's plans just hit a snag: The company must find some new names.
As spotted by Sean O'Kane at TechCrunch
, the United States Patent and Trademark Office has informed Tesla that it will not be allowed to trademark the word "robotaxi" to describe the vehicle.
According to the USPTO, the term is far too generic. Indeed, a
Google n-gram
search
shows a steady growth in the use of "robotaxi" starting more than a decade ago.
According to the USPTO, the term is merely descriptive.
The agency cites
evidence from Wikipedia, The Verge, and the Amazon-backed autonomous vehicle startup Zoox in its denial of Tesla's trademark application.
Maybe they should just have called it the Teslapod.
Credit:
David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images
Tesla could challenge this decision, but it would have to show the USPTO all the product's marketing materials, brochures, and manuals that intend to use the name. If those aren't available, Tesla must explain to the patent and trademark office's satisfaction how this product will differ from others, with detailed specifics, not generalities. Tesla must also explain whether the car features robotic systems and whether any of Tesla's competitors use "robo," "robot," or "robotic" to describe their own goods and services—the fact that Zoox refers to its autonomous pods as robotaxis will be very inconvenient for Tesla.
It's not the first time that Tesla has been accused of a lack of originality.
Alcon Entertainment sued Warner Brothers and Tesla
after it refused them permission and adamantly objected to WB's and Tesla's attempt to link the vehicle with vehicles seen in
Blade Runner 2049
. Although Tesla attempted to get the case dismissed, in April, the court ordered the parties to
enter into mediation
.
Nope, that’s not original, either
Perhaps even more inconveniently for Tesla, it will have to find a new name for the car itself. Tesla's attempt to trademark "Cybercab"
was also rejected
in large part due to the potential for confusion. Although Tesla applied for a trademark last October after revealing the vehicle,
several other companies have previously registered Cyber- prefix trademarks
, including one for "Cybercab" issued earlier in 2024.
The vehicle has neither room nor controls for a safety operator.
Credit:
Sjoerd van der Wal/Getty Images
Next month
, Tesla intends to deploy the two-seat EVs to Austin, Texas. The vehicles lack an actual steering wheel, so they won't conduct this testing with human safety operators on board; instead, Tesla will rely on teleoperation to handle problems that are too complicated for its AV stack to work out.
Those operators will probably be quite busy—last year, independent testing showed that Tesla's "FSD" system averaged one human intervention every 13 miles, and there
are numerous open investigations
by the National Traffic Highway Safety Administration into Tesla's driver assist systems, which only use monovision optical cameras and can be fooled by bright sunlight—and even, like Wile E. Coyote,
a painting of a road
.
Then again, perhaps as boss of DOGE, Musk will just use his "special government employee" status
to bring the USPTO to heel
, purging it of the experts needed to regulate his business,
just as he did at NHTSA
.
Jonathan M. Gitlin
Automotive Editor
Jonathan M. Gitlin
Automotive Editor
Jonathan is the Automotive Editor at Ars Technica. He has a BSc and PhD in Pharmacology. In 2014 he decided to indulge his lifelong passion for the car by leaving the National Human Genome Research Institute and launching Ars Technica's automotive coverage. He lives in Washington, DC.

data.title: Users advised to review Oracle Java use as Big Red's year end approaches
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 随着甲骨文（Oracle）财年末临近，专家警告用户可能面临更多Java软件审计。自2023年1月起，Oracle将Java许可模式从按用户收费改为按员工收费，导致客户成本增加两到五倍。许多企业正考虑转向开源Java替代方案，如OpenJDK，以避免高额费用和复杂的许可问题。Azul公司推出工具帮助企业跟踪Java实例，并发现越来越多用户计划切换到开放Java版本。咨询公司建议企业提前准备，考虑替代方案，以便在与Oracle谈判中占据有利位置。如果不续订Oracle Java，企业有可能摆脱许可困扰。

43936952.article_content:
Software
5
Users advised to review Oracle Java use as Big Red's year end approaches
5
International Java sales operation and the prospects of audits per-employee license model make the move to open source irresistible
Lindsay Clark
Fri 9 May 2025
//
13:35 UTC
Experts are warning of an increase in Oracle Java audits - as the tech giant nears its year end - following a switch to a per-employee license model that could see costs grow by up to five times.
Lords of May-hem: Seven signs it is Oracle's year end
READ MORE
Oracle introduced a paid subscription for Java in September 2018, and in
January 2023
decided to switch its pricing model to per employee rather than per user, creating a steep price hike for customers. In July 2023,
Gartner recorded users experiencing
price increases of between two and five times when they switched to the new licensing model.
Speaking to
The Register
, Scott Sellers, CEO of Java advisory and services company Azul, said: "We're definitely seeing an uptick. One of the things that seems to be happening is we're seeing more presence in more and more countries."
He told us Oracle is "putting specific Java sales teams in country, and then identifying those companies that appear to be downloading and... then going in and requesting to [do] audits. That recipe appears to be playing out truly globally at this point."
Oracle typically ramps up both
official and unofficial audits
at the end of its financial year, as its compliance teams assist in getting software deals over the line by the annual deadline. Since the shift in licensing terms, Java has also become part of that strategy. However it is also a time when users can consider their position.
"At the end of May, many of those existing contracts with Oracle are coming due, so companies are looking at whether or not it makes sense for them to continue to do business with Oracle or look for alternatives," Sellers said. There are also cases where customers have been able to keep their old pricing by negotiating with Oracle.
Counting Mastercard, Starbucks and HSBC among its customers, Azul has announced a tool, JVM Inventory, designed to offer runtime-level visibility to help classify and track Oracle Java instances. Earlier this year
a report from Dimensional Research
— sponsored by Azul — found the percentage of Oracle Java users considering switching to alternative JVMs or JDKs based an open approach increased from 72 percent in 2023 to 88 percent in 2024.
Craig Guarente, founder and CEO of Palisade Compliance, said companies should consider moving off of Oracle Java to get rid of the licensing problem. Even if they don't, considering the option could put them in a stronger position if they want to keep the old per-user license model.
"If you have no right in your contract to renew, that's really hard for customers because it doesn't say 'when this thing expires, you can do this other thing.' What they need to do is prepare early and to be able to move off of Oracle Java, at least the paid versions of it.
"So if you can put yourself in a position with Oracle to say, we actually don't need your product, you don't have to pay for it at all. That's when we see Oracle really negotiate with customers. If you can say to them 'How about I give you nothing?' if you have a credible alternative to what Oracle is proposing, then Oracle will move the needle," he said.
Eric Guyer, founding partner at Oracle and SAP advisory and consulting firm Remend, said Oracle had set up sales teams on Java separately from the main enterprise account management and audit function.
Only 1 in 10 Oracle Java users want to stay with Big Red
Oracle's Java pricing brews bitter taste, subscribers spill over to OpenJDK
'We had to educate Oracle about our contract,' CIO says after Big Red audit
Oracle Java police start knocking on Fortune 200's doors for first time
He said organizations comfortable with their compliance should be wary of returning the call.
"Oracle is going to call you. They're going to try and escalate the matter reach into your executive, and tell them that you're stealing millions of dollars of software if you don't return the phone calls. The recommendation is send those to your spam folder; just block it. Returning that phone call is admitting you need it. The average Java rep probably has 1,000 other companies on their list. They will move on to someone who does return that phone call," he said.
Guyer said few of his clients license Oracle Java, as Remend recommends companies move off it onto open source alternatives.
The Register
has asked Oracle to comment. ®

data.title: 37signals Says Goodbye to AWS: Full S3 Migration and $10M in Projected Savings
data.author: bluedino
data.article_summary: 软件公司37signals（知名于Basecamp和HEY等生产力工具）宣布完成从亚马逊云服务（AWS）的大规模迁移，将约18PB的数据转移到自建基础设施上，预计每年可节省超过1000万美元。此前，该公司每年在AWS S3存储上的花费约为150万美元，而自建基础设施的年成本不到20万美元。AWS承担了约25万美元的数据迁移费用。公司CTO David Heinemeier Hansson表示，公有云并非万能解决方案，自建硬件不仅可行而且更具成本效益。此次迁移也反映了越来越多企业重新评估对AWS、Azure等超大规模云服务的依赖，转向混合云或私有云以获得更多控制权和成本可预测性。欧洲IaaS提供商Stackscale等公司正通过私有云和裸机解决方案满足这一需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：云基础设施的成本与管理，特别是AWS等云服务提供商的高成本与自建基础设施的比较。

不同观点：
• [rthnbgrredf] 认为18PB的存储量不小，强调了维护大规模基础设施所需的工程努力和总拥有成本（TCO），指出简单的硬件租赁成本比较并不能反映实际的运行成本。便宜的硬件租赁虽然比主要云服务商便宜，但这并不是新发现。

• [bcoughlan] 提出将基础设施成本视为每个用户的成本，认为虽然成本看似巨大，但如果能够通过节省来服务大量用户，对公司的底线是有利的。同时指出迁移的机会成本，迁移过程中投入的人力本可以用于其他创收项目。

• [cube00] 批评AWS的定价变得贪婪，认为随着用户被锁定，AWS应该利用其规模来降低成本，而不是让自建基础设施更昂贵。并指出多年前迁移到云时看似更便宜。

• [troyvit] 对一家公司通过迁移基础设施节省超过1000万美元表示兴趣，并希望了解更多细节。其较小的组织坚持使用S3是因为觉得租用基础设施管理比自己雇佣人员更划算。

• [Imustaskforhelp] 寻求更容易的云迁移和多云策略，提到37Signals在多个国家设置服务器以减少延迟，但很多公司无法做到。同时比较了S3、Cloudflare R2、Wasabi和Backblaze的定价，认为根据访问频率选择不同服务商可能更优化。

• [datadrivenangel] 指出迁移出S3花了约2年时间，认为从计算和托管服务迁移的ROI虽然存在，但S3在商业上仍然很出色。

• [WD-42] 对支付租金给运行自己软件的服务商感到厌倦，认为自建基础设施是摆脱这种依赖的好方法。

• [RaSoJo] 对同一技术团队在迁移到自建基础设施后仍能管理所有事务表示惊讶，质疑是否需要额外的人手来处理安全和维护等工作。

The company led by David Heinemeier Hansson (DHH) completes its cloud repatriation by moving 18 PB of data to its own infrastructure. AWS covers the $250,000 egress cost.
Software company 37signals — creator of Basecamp, HEY, and other productivity tools — has officially begun migrating its data off Amazon Web Services (AWS), completing one of the most high-profile cloud repatriation efforts in recent years. According to a
LinkedIn post
by CTO David Heinemeier Hansson, the company is transferring all its data hosted on Amazon S3 to a new Pure Storage-based infrastructure deployed across its own data centers.
Ending Over a Decade on S3: Goodbye to $1.5M Annual Storage Bills
After over ten years using Amazon S3,
37signals plans to fully delete its AWS accounts this summer
. The migration includes about 18 petabytes of data being relocated to a high-performance flash system hosted in two company-controlled data centers. The current S3 storage cost is approximately $1.5 million per year, while their in-house infrastructure will cost less than $200,000 annually once the hardware is amortized.
The company also confirmed that AWS has covered the entire data transfer out (DTO) cost — around $250,000 — in line with its public commitment following the implementation of the EU Data Act, which mandates that cloud providers must eliminate technical and financial barriers to migration.
Full Control with In-House Infrastructure
37signals’ new strategy revolves around operating its own data centers, equipped with Pure Storage systems and Dell hardware. These centers will host all company data and applications. Initial investments, such as the $700,000 spent on hardware in 2023, have already been offset thanks to the gradual reduction in cloud-related commitments.
The company estimates it will save more than $10 million over the next five years, reducing its annual infrastructure bill from $3.2 million to less than $1 million — all managed by the same technical team that previously handled the cloud.
37signals Says Goodbye to AWS: Full S3 Migration and $10M in Projected Savings
Why Move Away from Public Cloud?
Although the decision has sparked debate, DHH remains clear: the public cloud isn’t a one-size-fits-all solution.
“The cloud can be great in some circumstances, but the industry convinced everyone it was the only viable option. We’re showing that running your own hardware is not only possible — it’s profitable.”
This sentiment resonates with a growing number of organizations reevaluating their dependence on hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud. Concerns around unpredictable costs, latency, data control, and budget predictability are fueling this “cloud repatriation” trend.
Stackscale: A European Private Cloud Alternative
Cases like 37signals are shining a spotlight on hybrid and private cloud infrastructure models, where customers can gain full control without sacrificing scalability or expert support.
In this landscape,
Stackscale
(Grupo Aire), a European infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) provider, offers
private cloud, bare-metal, and enterprise virtualization solutions
from data centers in Spain (Madrid and Alicante) and the Netherlands (Amsterdam), with a strong emphasis on availability, performance, and regulatory compliance.
According to
David Carrero
, co-founder and VP of Sales at Stackscale:
“We’re seeing more companies rethink their cloud strategies. Public cloud offers agility and elasticity, but for many high-volume or predictable workloads, our private solutions deliver over 40% cost savings, better performance, and stronger data sovereignty.”
Key Stackscale differentiators include:
Dedicated servers and bare-metal nodes without virtualization overhead
High-capacity redundant connectivity with low latency
GDPR-compliant privacy and data protection policies
Predictable flat-rate pricing with no hidden fees for traffic, IOPS, or snapshots
Human, expert, and local technical support
Conclusion: The Future of Infrastructure is Hybrid and Tailored
The 37signals case makes it clear that
cloud is not a static decision
. As businesses evolve, so must their infrastructure strategies. For many, the path forward involves
exclusive infrastructure, geographic proximity, and reduced reliance on hyperscalers
.
Private and hybrid cloud models are becoming strategic options, particularly in sectors like eCommerce, SaaS, fintech, media, and gaming. Long-term, controlling your hardware, owning your data, and enabling rapid adaptation can be a true competitive advantage.
As Carrero aptly puts it:
“This isn’t about going backwards — it’s about moving toward more efficient, sustainable, and transparent mod

data.title: Physicists turn lead into gold – for a fraction of a second
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 物理学家在大型强子对撞机（LHC）中实现了炼金术士的梦想，将铅离子转变为金，但这一过程仅持续百万分之一秒。在CERN，研究人员通过将铅离子以接近光速碰撞，利用其周围强烈的电磁场产生能量脉冲，使铅核射出三个质子，从而变成金。ALICE实验在2015至2018年间记录到860亿个金核的产生，总重量约为29万亿分之一克。这些不稳定的金原子很快解体或撞击实验设备。

不同观点：

LHC experiments don’t create large gold nuggets — but some particles within a beam of lead ions can turn into gold for about a microsecond.
Credit: Zen Rial/Getty
The dream of
seventeenth-century alchemists
has been realized by physicists at the
Large Hadron Collider
(LHC), who have turned lead into gold — albeit for only a fraction of a second and at tremendous cost.
The not-so-mysterious transmutation happened at CERN, Europe’s particle-physics laboratory, near Geneva, Switzerland, where the multi-billion-dollar LHC smashes together ions of lead for a portion of each experimental run.
How the revamped Large Hadron Collider will hunt for new physics
Early chemists hoped to turn abundant lead into precious gold. But differences in proton number between the elements (82 for lead and 79 for gold) made that impossible by chemical means.
CERN researchers achieved the feat by aiming beams of lead at each other, travelling at close to the speed of light. The ions occasionally glance past each other, rather than hit head on. When this happens, the intense electromagnetic field around an ion can create a pulse of energy that triggers an oncoming lead nucleus to eject three protons — turning it into gold.
The LHC’s ALICE experiment filtered out these instances of transmutation from the wider collision debris. In an analysis published on 7 May in
Physical Review Journals
1
, the team calculated that between 2015 and 2018, collisions at the LHC created 86 billion gold nuclei — around 29 trillionths of a gram. Most of the unstable, fast-moving gold atoms would have lasted around 1 microsecond before smashing into experimental apparatus or breaking into other particles.
The ALICE detector at CERN.
Credit: Maximillien Brice/CERN

data.title: Apple: "millions to billions" lost without App Store commissions
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 苹果公司正在紧急申请暂停执行上周法院对其反垄断行为的裁定，该裁定要求苹果允许开发者通过外部支付方式进行应用内购买，不再对其平台支付系统进行控制。法院认为苹果故意不遵守2021年的禁令，导致对其施加了新的限制，包括禁止控制平台支付和收取佣金。苹果已修改App审核指南，允许开发者添加外部支付链接，但公司认为新规将导致其每年损失巨额收入，并破坏iOS生态系统的完整性。苹果正在寻求上诉，并希望在此期间暂停执行该裁定。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对App Store现有模式和法院裁决影响的讨论

不同观点：
• Kon-Peki认为，开发者选择外部支付提供商（收取3-5%费用）将使他们不再使用Apple的支付系统（收取15-30%费用）。这可能导致App Store的现有形式难以维持。Kon-Peki还提出了几种可能的应对方式，包括取消第一方App Store、大幅提高年度开发者费用，或对免费应用的下载收取每GB费用。

• bradhe以另一种方式表达了类似观点，指出如果法院裁决生效，苹果从开发者那里获得的巨额收入将被返还，意味着苹果将失去一大收入来源。

• buyucu对裁决表示支持，认为开发者不再需要支付高额费用是件好事，表明了对开发者有利的立场。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于App Store的支付系统和收费模式。苹果通过其支付系统收取较高费用是争论的核心。开发者可能转向更便宜的外部支付系统，而这将对苹果的商业模式产生重大影响。

• 讨论还涉及到未来可能的替代方案，如改变App Store的运营模式或调整收费结构，以应对裁决带来的变化。这些方案对开发者和苹果的长期影响尚不明确，但引发了广泛的讨论。

Many horses, including
Spotify
and
Amazon's Kindle Store
, have already left the barn. But Apple is moving quickly to shut the external payments door opened by
last week's ruling
that the company willfully failed to comply with court orders regarding anticompetitive behavior.
In
an emergency motion filing late Wednesday
(PDF), Apple described US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers' "extraordinary Order" as including an injunction that "permanently precludes Apple from exercising control over core aspects of its business operations, including charging for use of its property and protecting the integrity of its platform and in-app purchase mechanism." A
certificate
(PDF) accompanying the emergency filing states that the order "fundamentally changes Apple's business and creates destabilizing effects" for App Store customers.
The restrictions, "which will cost Apple substantial sums annually," are not based on the company's conduct, Apple claims, but "were imposed to punish Apple for purported non-compliance" with the 2021 injunction. In
her ruling
(PDF), Gonzalez Rogers described Apple as conducting an "obvious cover-up" and said that Apple "at every turn chose the most anticompetitive option."
Apple had already altered its
App Review Guidelines
to comply with Gonzalez Rogers' ruling. Under the updated rules, developers have been able to include buttons, links, and calls to action to consider purchasing subscriptions and in-app payments through external sites and vendors. Apps like Spotify and Amazon's Kindle have already placed buttons and had their updates approved by Apple, and vendors like Stripe have been providing guidance on taking payments without Apple's commission. Before this, under a
2021 injunction
at issue in recent filings, Apple
charged a 12 to 27 percent commission
on external payments, with significant filing and auditing requirements.
Epic, whose lawsuit against Apple following
Fortnite
's removal from the App Store
kicked off this yearslong legal battle, complained about Apple's restrictions on external payment methods. That led to Gonzalez Rogers' order, which found that Apple "willfully" failed to comply with her 2021 injunction and referred the matter to federal prosecutors for potential criminal charges. Apple’s motion seeks to stay the injunctive opening of its App Store to external payments while it prepares its appeal.
Apple argued in its emergency motion last night that its appeal would show that it complied with the 2021 injunction "by allowing iOS app developers to convey information to users about alternative purchase options." Apple argues that the original injunction "says nothing about commissions or pricing," nor about conditions for link placement and language.
"The new rules profoundly undercut the integrated iOS ecosystem that this Court sustained as lawful and that is the foundation of user trust and confidence in the App Store," Apple's motion reads. Compliance with the order would cost "hundreds of millions to billions" of dollars, "which Apple can never recoup," Apple argues.

data.title: Ask HN: What are good high-information density UIs (screenshots, apps, sites)?
data.author: troupo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高信息密度的用户界面（UI）设计及其应用

不同观点：
• abound认为McMaster-Carr网站虽然不是信息最密集的，但其设计简洁、功能齐全，能够一次性展示大量信息，适合用户使用。
• chromy提供了多种用于追踪/分析/二进制分析的UI工具，以及3D建模和CAD软件（如Blender、Rhino）和音频编辑软件（DAWs），并提供了相关资源链接。
• mg介绍了自己开发的"product charts"项目，该项目通过双参数排序（如价格和发布日期）来展示产品信息，适合在大屏幕显示器上展示高密度的产品图表，而在移动设备上则使用普通列表。
• paddy_m区分了"Trader UI"和"VC UI"，前者强调高信息密度，适合交易员使用，后者则注重美观和简洁，适合风投支持的公司使用，并介绍了自己开发的Buckaroo项目。
• thih9指出专业创意人员使用的软件通常具有高信息密度和良好的用户体验，例如Blender这样的工具。
• jedberg怀念过去更高密度的UI设计，例如旧版Reddit移动界面，认为其信息展示更加高效。
• foobarbecue介绍了NASA JPL使用的工具，特别是RSVP Hyperdrive，并表示希望未来能开源该工具。
• fauria提到了命令行系统监控工具，如htop、atop、btop等，这些工具也具有高信息密度。
• coffeeindex提到了日本新闻网站和一般新闻网站的高密度UI设计，如Asahi、Yahoo、Bloomberg等。
• kccqzy介绍了Charles Schwab和Interactive Brokers的交易平台，这些平台为日内交易员和高端零售投资者设计，具有高信息密度和复杂的功能需求。
• roeles提到了现代战斗机驾驶舱的高密度UI设计，如Saab Gripen和F-35 JSF。
• smoe认为Ableton Live数字音频工作站具有高信息密度，且具有可折叠的嵌套部分，适合专业用户使用。
• seanhunter认为Bloomberg是高密度UI设计的明显例子，高效但需要一定技能才能充分利用。
• sxp提到Edward Tufte关于高密度信息图的书籍，并询问是否有更新参考资料，推荐了Bret Victor的"MagicInk"。

补充讨论：
• 高信息密度UI在不同领域的应用，包括电子商务、专业软件、交易平台、新闻网站、命令行工具和航空航天工具等。
• 争议焦点在于高密度UI和简洁UI的平衡，一些用户（如交易员）偏好高密度信息展示，而另一些用户和公司（如风投支持的公司）则偏好简洁美观的UI设计。
• 高密度UI设计的效率和用户体验问题，一些用户认为高密度UI可以提高效率，但需要用户具备一定技能。
• 高密度UI设计的具体实现方式，包括双参数排序、动态展示、嵌套部分和命令行工具等。
